problem: Misinformation detection relies on identifying both factual inaccuracies and the misleading narratives deliberately embedded by creators, but vision-language models fail to understand creator intent in multimodal content.
approach: DeceptionDecoded introduces a large-scale benchmark of 12,000 image-caption pairs grounded in trustworthy articles, using an intent-guided simulation framework to model both desired influence and execution plans, then evaluates state-of-the-art VLMs on three intent-centric tasks.
contribution: Demonstrates that current VLMs struggle with intent reasoning and rely on shallow cues, establishing DeceptionDecoded as a foundation for developing intent-aware models for multimodal misinformation detection.

problem: When users reselect alternative frames from Live Photos as key photos, they suffer noticeable quality degradation because the video capture pipeline produces lower quality than the photo ISP pipeline.
approach: LiveMoments uses a two-branch neural network with reference guidance: the reference branch extracts structure and texture from the original high-quality key photo, and the main branch restores the reselected frame; a Motion Alignment module incorporates motion guidance for spatial alignment at latent and image levels.
contribution: LiveMoments significantly improves perceptual quality and fidelity over existing solutions, especially in scenes with fast motion or complex structures.

problem: Post-hoc explanation methods for neural networks often lack provable guarantees, and identifying cardinally-minimal feature subsets requires computationally infeasible worst-case exponential verification queries.
approach: For Neural Additive Models (NAMs), a new model-specific algorithm generates provably cardinally-minimal explanations using only logarithmic verification queries after a parallelized preprocessing step on each univariate component.
contribution: Enables efficient generation of cardinally-minimal explanations for NAMs while providing smaller and faster explanations than existing subset-minimal explanation algorithms.

problem: Existing text-to-image model evaluation relies on single scalar quality scores, limiting comprehensive and interpretable feedback on image quality for preference alignment.
approach: ImageDoctor uses a vision-language model trained via supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to assess image quality across four dimensions (plausibility, semantic alignment, aesthetics, overall quality) with pixel-level flaw heatmaps using a look-think-predict paradigm.
contribution: Achieves strong alignment with human preference and improves T2I generation quality by 10% over scalar-based reward models when used for preference tuning.

problem: Large language models require substantial computational resources for deployment, and best practices for layer pruning combined with effective fine-tuning methods remain unclear.
approach: After extensive benchmarking, the paper shows that pruning final layers followed by fine-tuning lm_head and the remaining last three layers is remarkably effective, supported by gradient flow analysis.
contribution: Surpasses existing state-of-the-art pruning methods by 5.62%-17.27% on Llama-3.1-8B-It, 2.36%-19.45% on Llama-3-8B and 4.34%-9.59% on Llama-3-70B.

problem: Concept drift makes trained predictors unreliable, yet deciding when to retrain and what post-drift data size is sufficient remains rarely addressed.
approach: CALIPER is a detector and model-agnostic test that runs single-pass weighted local regression over post-drift windows and tracks one-step proxy error as a function of locality parameter to estimate required post-drift data size.
contribution: CALIPER consistently matches or exceeds the best fixed data size for retraining across heterogeneous datasets, learner families, and detectors while incurring negligible overhead.

problem: Large language models remain increasingly susceptible to jailbreaking in multi-turn scenarios where harmful intent can be subtly injected across conversations.
approach: PLAGUE is a plug-and-play framework inspired by lifelong-learning agents that divides multi-turn attacks into three phases (Primer, Planner, Finisher) to systematically explore the multi-turn attack family.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art jailbreaking results with attack success rates improved by more than 30% across leading models, achieving 81.4% on OpenAI's o3 and 67.3% on Claude's Opus 4.1.

problem: Real-time TDDFT requires time-consuming propagation of all occupied electronic states with fine time steps to predict molecular properties from external excitations.
approach: OrbEvo uses an equivariant graph transformer to learn full electronic wavefunction coefficient evolution over time, with equivariant conditioning for external fields and two variants (OrbEvo-WF and OrbEvo-DM) using wavefunction pooling and density matrix aggregation.
contribution: Demonstrates learning of time evolution operators for molecular wavefunctions with error accumulation mitigation during autoregressive rollout on a 5,000 molecule QM9 dataset.

problem: Visual instruction tuning datasets consist of randomly sampled image-question pairs without regard to informativeness, requiring large data budgets for effective multimodal model fine-tuning.
approach: COMPACT synthesizes rich and informative text questions for each image by combining multiple atomic visual capabilities in single training examples, reducing training data budget through task complexity scaling.
contribution: Reduces VIT data budget by 90% while achieving 100.2% of full VIT performance and improves performance on complex benchmarks like MM-Vet (+8.6%) and MMStar (+2.9%).

problem: Neural combinatorial optimization struggles to balance local construction scalability and global prediction constraint satisfaction when handling hard constraints.
approach: NEXCO integrates adaptive expansion natively into a diffusion framework as an intrinsic decoding principle, using a time-agnostic GNN denoiser and confidence-based solution expansion with feasibility projection.
contribution: Enables adaptive control over intermediate solution states during inference while maintaining constraint feasibility for combinatorial optimization problems.

problem: Existing VAE-based visual representation learning struggles to capture spatial correlations between objects or events, focusing instead on pixel intensities.
approach: Spatially informed VAEs (SI-VAE) use stochastic point processes and Papangelou conditional intensity as a self-supervision target to learn interpretable representations of spatial localization patterns.
contribution: Improves classification accuracy of attractive, repulsive, and uncorrelated point patterns from 48% (VAE) to over 80% in worst case and 90% in best case, enabling zero-shot conditional simulation from images.

problem: Automated formalization faces model hallucination and semantic gaps from ambiguous or missing premises in natural language descriptions of mathematical statements.
approach: CRAMF enhances LLM-based autoformalization by retrieving formal definitions of core mathematical concepts from an automatically constructed Mathlib4 knowledge base with contextual query augmentation and dual-channel hybrid retrieval.
contribution: Enables seamless integration into LLM-based autoformalizers with consistent improvements across miniF2F, ProofNet, and a newly proposed AdvancedMath benchmark.

problem: Current benchmarks for verifiable code generation focus on individual components rather than providing holistic evaluation of code, specification, and proof generation together.
approach: VERINA is a high-quality benchmark with 189 manually curated Lean coding tasks including problem descriptions, reference implementations, formal specifications, and test suites enabling comprehensive modular evaluation.
contribution: Reveals significant challenges in verifiable code generation, with the best model (OpenAI o3) achieving 72.6% code correctness, 52.3% specification soundness, and only 4.9% proof success rate.

problem: LLMs struggle with high-precision tasks like numerical computation and formal symbolic manipulation despite progress in mathematical reasoning.
approach: THOR integrates external tools via a multi-agent pipeline (TIRGen) that constructs tool-integrated reasoning datasets and an RL strategy optimizing both episode-level problem solving and step-level code generation with self-correction via tool feedback.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on mathematical benchmarks for models of similar scale with consistent improvements on code benchmarks.

problem: LoRA parameters cannot be transferred across different model backbones because they are dependent on the base model, limiting reusability of fine-tuned adapters.
approach: TiTok enables LoRA transplantation through token-wise contrastive excess between source models with and without LoRA, highlighting informative tokens and enabling selective filtering of synthetic data without additional models.
contribution: Achieves average performance gains of +4-8% across three benchmarks in multiple transfer settings without requiring additional discriminator models.

problem: Scaling laws research has focused overwhelmingly on English despite most prominent AI models serving billions of international users with multiple languages.
approach: ATLAS introduces adaptive transfer scaling laws based on 774 multilingual training experiments spanning 10M-8B parameters and 400+ training languages, deriving cross-lingual transfer matrices and language-agnostic scaling laws.
contribution: Outperforms existing scaling laws' generalization often by more than 0.3 R-squared and reveals computational crossover points for when to pretrain from scratch versus finetune from multilingual checkpoints.

problem: LLM training processes vast corpora in single pass, leaving available data underutilized, and the tradeoff between repeated epochs on same data versus fresh samples is theoretically unclear.
approach: Theoretical analysis characterizes scaling behavior of effective data reuse rate E(K,N) for multi-epoch training using SGD in linear regression under strong convexity or Zipf-distributed data.
contribution: Proves that small K yields linear gains (E ≈ K) while larger K plateaus at problem-dependent values Θ(log N), explaining why larger datasets can be repeated more before marginal benefit vanishes.

problem: DR-submodular maximization with realistic stochastic biased gradients remains challenging, and existing methods assume unbiased gradient noise.
approach: Generalizes the Lyapunov framework to biased stochastic gradients, considers convex sets with largest element constraints, and proposes both classical zero-order algorithms with O(ε^-3) and quantum algorithms with O(ε^-1) iteration complexity.
contribution: Provides 1/e approximation algorithm for non-monotone DR-submodular maximization under novel constraints, surpassing the hardness result 1/4 for general convex constraints, with quantum acceleration validated numerically.

problem: Binary verifier feedback in reasoning post-training is brittle because many tasks admit partially correct answers that verifiers under-credit, limiting learning from nuanced supervisory signals.
approach: HERO integrates sparse verifier signals with dense reward model scores using stratified normalization to bound scores within verifier-defined groups and variance-aware weighting to emphasize challenging prompts.
contribution: Consistently outperforms reward model-only and verifier-only baselines across mathematical reasoning benchmarks with strong gains on both verifiable and hard-to-verify tasks.

problem: Fixed block size in semi-autoregressive diffusion LLM decoding suffers from late decoding overhead on high-confidence tokens and premature errors on low-confidence tokens.
approach: AdaBlock-dLLM identifies a volatility band region during denoising that encodes local semantic structure and uses it as a training-free scheduler to adaptively adjust block size during runtime.
contribution: Achieves up to 5.3% accuracy improvement under the same throughput budget through semantic-aware adaptive block sizing.

problem: Current evaluation benchmarks do not adequately assess LLM agents' ability to solve real-world tasks requiring synthesis of information from multiple sources and inferring insights.
approach: DEEPSYNTH is a benchmark with 120 tasks across 7 domains and 42 countries designed using multi-stage data collection requiring annotators to collect official sources, create hypotheses, and perform manual analysis.
contribution: Demonstrates that state-of-the-art LLMs and agents achieve maximum F1 of 8.97, revealing that current agents struggle with hallucinations and reasoning over large information spaces.

problem: Machine unlearning in high-dimensional regimes where p~n lacks theoretical analysis because standard optimization assumptions rarely hold simultaneously.
approach: Introduces ε-Gaussian certifiability tailored to high-dimensional regimes and theoretically analyzes Newton-method-based unlearning showing that one step plus calibrated Gaussian noise suffices for privacy and accuracy.
contribution: Achieves privacy and accuracy in high-dimensional unlearning with single Newton step, contrasting with prior work requiring two steps, demonstrating improved efficiency in proportional regimes.

problem: Vision language models cannot form robust spatial mental models from limited views like humans do, exhibiting near-random performance on spatial reasoning.
approach: MindCube benchmark with 21,154 questions evaluates VLM spatial mental modeling through position (cognitive mapping), orientation (perspective-taking), and dynamics tasks; proposes map-then-reason approach combining cognitive map generation with reasoning.
contribution: Map-then-reason boosts accuracy from 37.8% to 60.8% (+23%), with reinforcement learning pushing to 70.7% (+32.9%), demonstrating that internal structured spatial representations improve understanding of unobservable space.

problem: Large protein complexes exceed quadratic memory scaling limits of end-to-end neural network inference, making structure prediction impractical for complexes beyond a few thousand tokens.
approach: HierAFold exploits modularity via PAE-guided subunit decomposition, performs targeted interface-aware refinement, and uses confidence-weighted assembly to enable hierarchical structure prediction.
contribution: Matches AlphaFold3 accuracy while raising success rates from 49.9% to 73.1% on recent PDB set, cuts peak memory by ~25GB (~40%), and successfully models complexes over 5,000 tokens.

problem: Static world models fail when confronted with novel or rare configurations, limiting their ability to adapt to new environments.
approach: Formalizes in-context learning of world models identifying two mechanisms: environment recognition (ER) and environment learning (EL), derives error upper-bounds exposing mechanism emergence, and empirically investigates how data distribution affects ICL.
contribution: Demonstrates distinct ICL mechanisms exist in world models with emergence depending on long context and diverse environments, highlighting self-adapting world model potential.

problem: Existing self-refinement methods use reactive processes with fixed iterations, making it difficult to determine optimal timing and content of refinement based on evolving generation context.
approach: ProActive Self-Refinement (PASR) enables LLMs to refine outputs during generation by proactively deciding whether, when, and how to refine based on internal state and evolving context.
contribution: Reduces average token consumption by 41.6% compared to standard generation while achieving 8.2% accuracy improvement on Qwen3-8B across diverse tasks.

problem: Existing sublinear spectral clustering oracles require Omega(sqrt n) memory for data structures, creating bottlenecks for massive graphs and memory-limited settings.
approach: Establishes memory-time tradeoffs for sublinear spectral clustering oracles on well-clusterable graphs, showing oracles can construct data structures using much smaller than O(sqrt n) memory (e.g. O(n^0.01)) while maintaining sublinear query time.
contribution: Breaks the Omega(sqrt n) memory barrier and characterizes near-optimal tradeoff frontiers, demonstrating trade-offs like S·T=Õ(n) for logarithmic conductance gap clustering.

problem: Continual test-time adaptation over long term suffers from model collapse and error accumulation, with existing reset strategies either using periodic resets independently of collapse or causing catastrophic knowledge loss.
approach: Proposes Adaptive and Selective Reset (ASR) that dynamically determines when and where to reset, importance-aware regularization to recover essential knowledge, and on-the-fly adaptation adjustment for domain shifts.
contribution: Demonstrates effectiveness across long-term TTA benchmarks with strong gains under challenging conditions through adaptive selective resets preserving beneficial knowledge.

problem: Geometric transformations in image editing pose challenges in accuracy of translation, rotation, and scaling, and existing approaches inadequately model intricate lighting and shadow effects.
approach: GeoEdit leverages in-context generation through diffusion transformers integrated with geometric transformations and introduces Effects-Sensitive Attention to model lighting and shadows; trained on RS-Objects dataset with 120,000 image pairs.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in visual quality, geometric accuracy, and realism on public benchmarks.

problem: LLM-based autoformalization lacks reliable semantic consistency checks to ensure formal code preserves meaning of original statements and cannot support iterative improvement through corrective feedback.
approach: LoC-Decomp integrates automatic semantic consistency checker and Lean 4 compiler for iterative refinement, uses COT-like decomposition template for modular formalization, and implements divide-conquer-merge semantic self-checking.
contribution: Enables iterative feedback-driven refinement leveraging semantic and syntactic error signals to guide progressive LLM formalization improvement.

problem: Centralized distributed optimization may not scale with number of workers once server-to-worker communication is accounted for, contrary to the motivation for distributed training.
approach: Establishes new lower bounds for federated learning considering both worker-to-server and server-to-worker communication, proving that accounting for server communication makes scaling infeasible.
contribution: Demonstrates fundamental limitations in centralized distributed optimization, showing that unbiased random sparsification alone cannot overcome server communication bottlenecks.

problem: Scientists manually develop computational tools for analyzing complex experimental data through iterative literature review and testing, a costly and time-consuming process.
approach: TusoAI is an agentic system that takes scientific task descriptions with evaluation functions and autonomously develops optimized computational methods, integrating domain knowledge into a knowledge tree with iterative domain-specific optimization.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art expert methods and scientific AI agents across diverse tasks and improves existing computational methods in genetics.

problem: Surgical triplet detection datasets like CholecT50 lack precise spatial bounding box annotations, limiting triplet classification from image-level to practical applications requiring spatial context.
approach: ProstaTD provides large-scale surgical triplet detection dataset from robot-assisted prostatectomy with 71,775 video frames from 21 surgeries, precise bounding box annotations, and a surgical triplet detection evaluation toolkit.
contribution: Provides clinically validated benchmark with high-precision annotations for surgical triplet detection including spatial context and created specialized annotation and evaluation tools.

problem: Semi-structured (N:M)-sparsity offers hardware-friendly LLM inference acceleration, but existing approaches either use rule-based layerwise greedy search with errors or gradient-driven combinatorial learning with prohibitive training costs.
approach: MaskPro proposes linear-space probabilistic framework learning prior categorical distributions for every M consecutive weights and introduces moving average tracker of loss residuals to mitigate high variance in policy gradients.
contribution: Demonstrates superior performance with excellent scalability in memory efficiency and robustness to data samples for (N:M)-sparsity on LLMs.

problem: Deep learning bioactivity prediction methods struggle with out-of-domain generalization and existing methods require access to source data, making them impractical when data cannot be accessed due to privacy or IP restrictions.
approach: Proposes uncertainty-weighted consistency strategy where high-confidence samples guide augmented counterparts by minimizing feature distance, integrated with contrastive optimization to prevent feature collapse.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines under scaffold, protein, and assay-based OOD settings without access to source data.

problem: Benchmarking hundreds of functional connectivity modeling methods on large-scale fMRI datasets is computationally prohibitive due to combinatorial explosion of model-data pairings.
approach: SCLCS proposes structure-aware contrastive learning framework selecting small representative core-sets that preserve relative performance ranking of FC operators, using adaptive Transformer and novel Structural Perturbation Score.
contribution: Preserves ground-truth model ranking with just 10% of data, outperforming state-of-the-art core-set selection by up to 23.2% in ranking consistency.

problem: LLM reasoning tasks suffer from hallucination and factual inconsistency in knowledge-intensive domains due to lack of external knowledge and factual verification.
approach: VoG framework enhances LLM reasoning via iterative retrieval, stepwise KG verification, and adaptive revision using context-aware multi-armed bandit strategy guided by reward signals capturing uncertainty and semantic consistency.
contribution: Consistently improves both reasoning accuracy and efficiency across three benchmark datasets through knowledge graph-augmented iterative verification and revision.

problem: Computing optimal matching in online stochastic matching is NP-hard, making online learning computationally infeasible without structural assumptions.
approach: Focuses on single-peaked preferences where users' preferences are unimodal, devises efficient algorithm for offline budgeted matching and leverages it into efficient online algorithm with PQ tree-based order approximation.
contribution: Achieves regret of Õ(U·√(TK)) when single-peaked structure is known, compared to Õ(UKT^2/3) without knowledge of structure.

problem: Current benchmarks for long-context reasoning blur critical factors like intrinsic task complexity, distractor interference, and task length, making failure analysis imprecise.
approach: CogniLoad generates natural-language logic puzzles with independently tunable parameters reflecting Cognitive Load Theory: intrinsic difficulty d, distractor-to-signal ratio ρ, and task length N.
contribution: Identifies task length as dominant constraint and reveals varied tolerances to intrinsic complexity and U-shaped responses to distractor ratios across 22 reasoning LLMs.

problem: Existing time series forecasting methods rely primarily on numerical data alone, ignoring multimodal information that could improve predictions on complex real-world patterns.
approach: VoT proposes Event-driven Reasoning combining exogenous text with LLM reasoning capabilities via Historical In-context Learning for guidance, and Multi-level Alignment integrating endogenous text at representation level and fusing frequency components.
contribution: Demonstrates significant improvements on real-world datasets across 10 domains, validating effectiveness of unlocking text value for time series forecasting.

problem: LLM inference cost grows prohibitively as models scale, and the trade-off between model accuracy and inference efficiency remains underexplored.
approach: We introduce a conditional scaling law that augments the Chinchilla framework with architectural information, analyzing how hidden size, MLP-to-attention ratio, and grouped-query attention influence both inference cost and accuracy, then use a search framework to identify optimal architectures.
contribution: Optimized architectures achieve up to 2.1% higher accuracy and 42% greater inference throughput compared to LLaMA-3.2 under the same training budget.

problem: Large language models encode social biases tied to sensitive features such as race and gender, and existing debiasing methods either require expensive fine-tuning, are architecture-specific, or fail to address multiple overlapping protected attributes.
approach: We propose multi-feature quantized attention regularization (MQAR) that injects structured quantization into frozen self-attention layers, using vector-quantized regularization and adversarial autoencoders to suppress protected-attribute information while preserving task semantics.
contribution: MQAR consistently reduces bias across multiple protected attributes on five LLMs (BERT, T5, GPT-Neo, Mixtral, LLaMA 3.2) while maintaining downstream accuracy within 0.4% of baseline.

problem: Existing video language model benchmarks assess overall performance across entire video sequences but overlook positional biases, a critical yet underexplored aspect of LVLM behavior.
approach: We introduce Video-LevelGauge, a dedicated benchmark with standardized probes and customized contextual setups that flexibly control context length, probe position, and contextual types, combined with statistical measures and bias pattern recognition.
contribution: Evaluation of 27 state-of-the-art LVLMs reveals significant positional biases in open-source models (head/neighbor-content preferences) while commercial models like Gemini 2.5 Pro show consistent performance across video sequences.

problem: Disentangled representations seek to recover latent factors of variation, yet their identifiability is not fully understood and relies on assumptions that may not hold.
approach: We introduce mechanistic independence, which characterizes latent factors by how they act on observed variables rather than by their latent distribution, proposing independence criteria ranging from support-based and sparsity-based to higher-order conditions.
contribution: These criteria yield identifiability of latent subspaces even under nonlinear, non-invertible mixing, and establish a hierarchy among criteria with graph-theoretic characterization of latent factors.

problem: Existing reward models follow either generative (costly point-wise supervision) or discriminative (uncalibrated scores) paradigms, neither capturing probabilistic quality assessment.
approach: We introduce Ordinal Probabilistic Reward Model (OPRM) which discretizes quality into ordinal ratings and learns a full probability distribution per response, combined with Region Flooding Tuning (RgFT) to concentrate probability mass within corresponding rating sub-regions.
contribution: Our method improves accuracy by 2.9% to 7.4% compared to prior reward models and captures both relative rankings and absolute quality.

problem: Existing reasoning-enhanced IR approaches face challenges in applicability, scalability, and efficiency when retrieving documents with implicit or indirect relevance to tasks.
approach: We propose Retro*, a rubric-based relevance scoring mechanism with test-time scaling via score integration of multiple reasoning trajectories, optimized with a novel reinforcement learning algorithm employing composite rewards.
contribution: Retro* achieves state-of-the-art performance on the BRIGHT benchmark, outperforming existing document retrieval methods.

problem: Climate data super-resolution struggles with high-frequency spatial information reconstruction, especially over complex terrain, because DNNs exhibit frequency bias and climate data is dominated by low-frequency components.
approach: GeoFAR explicitly encodes climatic patterns at different frequencies while learning implicit geographical neural representations (location and elevation), providing frequency-aware and geography-informed representations.
contribution: GeoFAR mitigates high-frequency prediction errors in both deterministic and generative SR models, achieving state-of-the-art performance across various spatial resolutions and downscaling ratios.

problem: Reasoning tasks are difficult because their latent space exceeds observation space complexity and latent variables are densely structured with strong dependencies, despite existing models failing to perform reasoning reliably.
approach: We cast reasoning as a selection mechanism and introduce SR², which incorporates estimated latent variables as feedback with three modules: reflective representation learning, dependency self-refinement, and periodic intermediate alignment.
contribution: The framework addresses reasoning task challenges by learning dense dependencies among latent representations.

problem: Neural network-based actor-critic models remain opaque black boxes, concealing decision-making processes and hindering their use in critical applications requiring transparent and explainable reasoning.
approach: We introduce an adaptation of the actor-critic framework that integrates rule ensembles for the actor while using neural networks for the critic, ensuring transparency and interpretability.
contribution: Our method matches or exceeds performance of representative RL models across seven classic and complex environments while offering self-interpretability and transparency.

problem: Estimating heterogeneous treatment effects in time-varying settings is challenged by severe overlap problems—the probability of observing certain treatment sequences decreases exponentially, leaving many sequences under-supported.
approach: We introduce overlap-weighted orthogonal (WO) meta-learner that targets regions with high probability of receiving interventional treatment sequences, developing a Neyman-orthogonal population risk function.
contribution: The WO-learner is Neyman-orthogonal (robust to nuisance misspecification), fully model-agnostic, and provides more reliable HTE estimates under low overlap conditions.

problem: Existing travel planning benchmarks operate on slot-filling paradigms restricted to synthetic queries with pre-defined constraint menus, failing to capture the open-ended, compositional, and implicit nature of real user requirements.
approach: We introduce ChinaTravel with a practical sandbox for multi-day travel planning, a compositionally generalizable domain-specific language for scalable evaluation, and an open-ended dataset from 1154 human participants.
contribution: Fine-grained analysis shows neuro-symbolic agents achieve 37.0% constraint satisfaction on human queries—a 10× improvement over purely neural models—highlighting challenges in compositional generalization.

problem: Selecting the best source domain and pre-trained model for domain adaptation is non-trivial due to lack of labeled validation data for the target domain and the large number of available pre-trained models.
approach: We propose PAS, a score designed to estimate transferability of a source domain and pre-trained feature extractor to a target task before adaptation, leveraging pre-trained models' generalization power and assessing source-target compatibility.
contribution: PAS correlates strongly with actual target accuracy and consistently guides selection of the best-performing pre-trained model and source domain for adaptation.

problem: Off-policy evaluation for ranking policies fails under deterministic logging policies because existing estimators (ranking-wise and position-wise IPS) require the logging policy to be sufficiently stochastic.
approach: We propose Click-based Inverse Propensity Score (CIPS) and Click-based Doubly Robust (CDR) estimators that exploit user click behavior's intrinsic stochasticity as importance weighting.
contribution: Our estimators achieve significantly lower bias than baselines, particularly under completely deterministic logging policies where existing methods incur substantial bias.

problem: Existing learning-based planning for autonomous driving follows a deterministic paradigm and fails to handle uncertainty and non-determinism inherent in real-world driving.
approach: We propose VADv2, a probabilistic planning model that discretizes the high-dimensional action space into a planning vocabulary, tokenizes it into planning tokens, and models the probabilistic distribution of actions.
contribution: VADv2 achieves state-of-the-art closed-loop performance on CARLA Town05 benchmark, significantly outperforming existing methods and demonstrating effectiveness on NAVSIM and 3DGS-based benchmarks.

problem: Wireless localization across diverse environments is challenging due to complex wireless signals and their sensitivity to environmental changes, with existing approaches suffering from limited generalization.
approach: We propose SigMap, a multimodal foundation model with cycle-adaptive masking based on channel periodicity and a map-as-prompt framework integrating 3D geographic information via soft prompts for cross-scenario adaptation.
contribution: SigMap achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple localization tasks with strong zero-shot generalization, significantly outperforming supervised and self-supervised baselines.

problem: Multi-agent reasoning systems are poorly understood—it is unclear when communication benefits performance and what tradeoffs exist between agent count, communication bandwidth, and problem complexity.
approach: We propose a theoretical framework analyzing expressivity of multi-agent systems across three algorithmic families (state tracking, recall, k-hop reasoning), deriving bounds on agents required, inter-agent communication, and achievable speedups.
contribution: Results identify regimes where communication is provably beneficial, delineate tradeoffs between agent count and bandwidth, and expose intrinsic limitations under resource constraints.

problem: Generative models typically require large, spatially redundant latent spaces, increasing training costs and architectural complexity.
approach: We introduce Representation Tokenizer (RepTok) which represents images using a single continuous latent token from pre-trained SSL encoders, fine-tuning only the token embedding with flow-matching and cosine-similarity regularization.
contribution: RepTok achieves competitive results on class-conditional ImageNet generation and zero-shot text-to-image synthesis on MS-COCO with extremely limited training budgets.

problem: Point cloud-based motion capture faces a tradeoff between point-based methods (geometrically detailed but noisy) and skeleton-based ones (robust but oversimplified) when handling noisy, unstructured point clouds.
approach: We propose Sparkle, a structured representation unifying skeletal joints and surface anchors with explicit kinematic-geometric factorization, learned through hierarchical modules embedding geometric continuity and kinematic constraints.
contribution: SparkleMotion achieves state-of-the-art performance in accuracy, robustness, and generalization under severe domain shifts, noise, and occlusion across diverse sensor types.

problem: Navigation foundation models trained on offline web-scale data lack capacity to reason about action consequences or adapt through counterfactual understanding, limiting real-world urban navigation.
approach: We introduce Seeing-to-Experiencing (S2E) framework combining offline pretraining via Anchor-Guided Distribution Matching with reinforcement learning via Residual-Attention Modules for reactive behaviors.
contribution: S2E maintains generalizability from large-scale pretraining while enhancing interactivity through RL, achieving state-of-the-art performance on NavBench-GS and real-world robustness assessments.

problem: Aligning LLMs with human preferences typically requires computationally intensive training or complex reward architectures.
approach: We introduce PALC (Preference Alignment via Logit Calibration), a parameter-efficient framework operating at the logit layer where each dimension corresponds to a token, using a bottleneck architecture to learn position-dependent calibration vectors.
contribution: PALC outperforms most test-time alignment methods while maintaining near-baseline inference speed and enabling runtime adjustment of alignment strength without retraining.

problem: The global convergence rates and practical efficiency of Newton methods for convex optimization remain underexplored, especially with modern stepsize schedules and linesearch procedures.
approach: We propose stepsize schedules and linesearch procedures with fast global convergence guarantees up to O(1/k^3) for convex functions with Hölder continuous Hessians or third derivatives.
contribution: We provide strong convergence guarantees for Newton method with exact linesearch, covering cases with multiple smoothness parameterizations or unknown smoothness constants.

problem: Determining appropriate neural network width under computational constraints is a fundamental challenge without a principled pre-training approach.
approach: We introduce a practical metric derived from Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) that estimates minimum network width by examining the smallest eigenvalue of the NTK at initialization.
contribution: Our NTK-based metric effectively identifies cardinal width—the width at which generalization performance saturates—across multiple datasets and architectures.

problem: Existing LLM training libraries lack easy-to-use abstractions for long-context training optimization, forcing users to manually compose complex optimizations requiring in-depth expertise.
approach: We introduce AutoSP, which automatically applies targeted optimizations: automated sequence parallelism and long-context-aware activation checkpointing.
contribution: AutoSP increases training contexts by up to 2.7× on NVIDIA and 2.5× on AMD hardware at negligible cost to runtime performance.

problem: Vision-Language Models show limited performance in 3D spatial comprehension critical for embodied intelligence, primarily due to lack of global-local correspondence between scenes and individual frames.
approach: We introduce GPT4Scene, a visual prompting paradigm that constructs a Bird's Eye View image from video and marks consistent object IDs across frames and BEV, enabling the model to build global-local relationships.
contribution: In zero-shot evaluation, GPT4Scene improves performance over closed-source VLMs like GPT-4o, and fine-tuning on 165K annotated videos achieves state-of-the-art on all 3D understanding tasks.

problem: LLMs exhibit strong but shallow alignment: they directly refuse harmful queries at the start but protection collapses once harmful continuation is underway.
approach: We propose Any-Depth Alignment (ADA), an inference-time defense that reintroduces assistant header tokens mid-stream, inducing the model to reassess harmfulness at any generation point.
contribution: ADA secures near-100% refusal rate against adversarial prefill attacks and reduces success rates of GCG, AutoDAN, PAIR, and TAP attacks to below 3%, all without modifying base model parameters.

problem: Existing personalized federated learning methods assume homogeneous data and models across clients, failing to address realistic scenarios with data and model heterogeneity.
approach: We propose FedMosaic, which addresses data and model heterogeneity with task-relevance-aware model aggregation and dimension-invariant modules enabling knowledge sharing across heterogeneous architectures.
contribution: FedMosaic outperforms state-of-the-art PFL methods in both personalization and generalization across 40 distinct tasks with distribution shifts over time.

problem: Meta learning faces training inefficiencies from numerous low-contribution tasks and noisy labels, yet lacks training data attribution methods due to the dual-layer structure complicating data contribution modeling.
approach: We propose a general data attribution framework within bilevel optimization, introducing task influence functions (task-IF) and instance influence functions (instance-IF) to assess impact across inner and outer training processes.
contribution: Our framework provides closed-form solutions for task and instance influence functions, with strategies to enhance computational efficiency and scalability.

problem: Diverse dataset distillation methods exist but their underlying connections remain largely unexplored, limiting understanding of what distillation fundamentally achieves.
approach: We introduce UniDD, a spectral filtering framework unifying diverse DD objectives by interpreting each as a filter applied to eigenvalues of the feature-feature correlation matrix.
contribution: UniDD reveals that DD fundamentally matches frequency-specific features and proposes Curriculum Frequency Matching (CFM) that gradually adjusts filter parameters to cover both low- and high-frequency information.

problem: Long video generation with Diffusion Transformers is bottlenecked by quadratic attention scaling, as attention is highly redundant and outputs are dominated by small query-key subsets.
approach: We introduce Mixture-of-Groups Attention (MoGA), using a lightweight learnable token router to precisely match tokens with semantic-aware routing, integrating seamlessly with FlashAttention and sequence parallelism.
contribution: An efficient long video generation model produces minute-level, multi-shot 480p videos at 24 fps with a context length of approximately 580k tokens.

problem: AI-generated images often exhibit subtle semantic anomalies like unrealistic object configurations, physical law violations, or commonsense inconsistencies that compromise plausibility.
approach: We introduce AnomReason, a large-scale benchmark with structured annotations (Name, Phenomenon, Reasoning, Severity) produced by a modular multi-agent pipeline (AnomAgent) with lightweight human verification.
contribution: Models fine-tuned on AnomReason achieve consistent gains on semantic matching metrics, with applications to explainable deepfake detection and semantic reasonableness assessment.

problem: 2D ultrasound interpretation is highly operator-dependent and cognitively demanding, hindering reproducibility and reliability of clinical diagnosis.
approach: We present UltraGauss, an ultrasound-specific Gaussian Splatting framework that renders via probe-plane intersection with in-plane aggregation, aligning with plane-based echo sampling.
contribution: UltraGauss delivers state-of-the-art 2D-to-3D reconstructions reaching 0.99 SSIM within approximately 20 minutes on a single GPU, with clinical expert surveys rating reconstructions the most realistic.

problem: Protein folding models typically employ complex domain-specific architectures with multiple training objectives, raising the question of whether these designs are truly necessary.
approach: We introduce SimpleFold, the first flow-matching based protein folding model using only general-purpose transformer blocks with adaptive layers and a generative objective plus structural term.
contribution: SimpleFold-3B achieves competitive performance on standard folding benchmarks and demonstrates strong ensemble prediction performance, challenging the reliance on complex domain-specific designs.

problem: Training transformers in low-precision settings with flash attention leads to catastrophic loss explosions, a long-standing and unresolved failure case.
approach: We provide mechanistic explanation revealing that failure is caused by emergence of similar low-rank representations in attention and compounding biased rounding errors, introducing a minimal modification to flash attention.
contribution: Our fix mitigates bias in rounding errors, stabilizing low-precision training and confirming our analysis of the underlying failure mechanism.

problem: Using full text corpora in LLM context windows is costly due to KV cache memory scaling with input length, limiting practical deployment.
approach: We introduce Cartridges, trained KV cache representations per corpus, loaded at inference time via self-study—a training recipe generating synthetic conversations and training with context-distillation.
contribution: Cartridges trained with self-study match in-context learning performance while using 38.6× less memory and enabling 26.4× higher throughput, extending effective context from 128k to 484k tokens.

problem: Transformer components like non-linear activations and normalization are non-injective, raising the possibility that different inputs map to the same output, preventing exact input recovery.
approach: We prove mathematically that transformer language models mapping discrete input sequences to continuous representations are injective and introduce SipIt, the first algorithm that provably and efficiently reconstructs exact input text from hidden activations.
contribution: Through billions of collision tests on six state-of-the-art LLMs, we confirm no collisions occur, establishing injectivity as a fundamental property with implications for transparency and safe deployment.

problem: Current learning algorithms for linear state-space models lack ability to learn system matrices with sparsity constraints due to similarity transformation complications.
approach: We impose sparsity-promoting priors on system matrices and explore the expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm to derive maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimates of both hidden states and system matrices.
contribution: The proposed algorithm converges to a local maximum or saddle point and preserves topological structure among variables while significantly improving prediction accuracy.

problem: Existing test-time compute allocation methods distribute compute uniformly across queries, overlooking variation in query difficulty and wasting resources on unsolvable instances.
approach: We formulate test-time compute allocation as a bandit learning problem, proposing adaptive algorithms that estimate query difficulty on-the-fly and prioritize solvable instances.
contribution: Our algorithms achieve up to 11.10% performance improvement on MATH-500, 10.82% on AIME25, and 11.23% on LiveCodeBench compared to uniform allocation.

problem: The robustness of video understanding models to domain shifts encountered in real-world applications remains critical yet underexplored, limiting practical reliability.
approach: We introduce VUDG, a dataset with 11 distinct domains covering three types of domain shifts while maintaining semantic consistency, plus a multi-expert progressive annotation framework for efficient labeling.
contribution: Evaluation of 9 representative LVLMs and traditional VQA methods shows most models suffer performance degradation under domain shifts, highlighting challenges in robustness.

problem: On-device learning requires training models directly on edge devices to cut energy and protect privacy, but expanding neural networks create memory bottlenecks for backpropagation.
approach: We apply subspace-based training to transformers through Weight-Activation Subspace Iteration (WASI), restricting training to fixed subspaces to mitigate memory bottlenecks.
contribution: WASI maintains comparable accuracy while reducing memory usage by up to 62× and computational cost by up to 2×, achieving 1.4× faster training on Raspberry Pi 5.

problem: Tensor decomposition methods for LLM compression face a dense core tensor bottleneck that grows polynomially with chosen ranks, capping achievable compression ratios.
approach: We introduce LeSTD (Learning-based Sparse Tensor Decomposition), a two-stage framework that identifies a high-quality shared orthogonal basis then applies importance-based pruning to learn ultra-sparse core tensors.
contribution: LeSTD breaks the compression ceiling imposed by dense cores, enabling significantly higher compression ratios than prior tensor decomposition methods.

problem: Text-to-speech systems struggle to efficiently condition diffusion models while removing computational bottlenecks from attention and recurrence modules, limiting deployment scalability.
approach: MambaVoiceCloning replaces attention-based conditioning with a fully state-space model (Mamba) architecture across text encoding, temporal modeling, and expressive prosody control, maintaining linear-time complexity with bounded memory.
contribution: Achieves statistically reliable quality gains over StyleTTS2 and VITS while reducing encoder parameters to 21M and improving throughput by 1.6x.

problem: Distributionally robust regression over grouped data remains computationally expensive when using interior point methods, requiring many linear system solves.
approach: Uses block Lewis weights to relate the group distributionally robust problem to a carefully chosen least squares formulation, then applies accelerated proximal methods.
contribution: Achieves (1+ε)-optimal solutions with improved complexity over interior point methods for moderate accuracy regimes.

problem: Large language models lack meaningful confidence estimates for the semantic content of their outputs, remaining uncertain whether base LLMs can assess meaning-level confidence beyond token prediction.
approach: Introduces B-calibration—a calibration framework parameterized by equivalence classes—and demonstrates that semantic calibration emerges from local loss optimality without explicit supervision.
contribution: Shows base LLMs are remarkably well-calibrated for semantic content in open-ended QA, while instruction-tuning and chain-of-thought reasoning systematically break this calibration.

problem: Multimodal large language models trained with reinforcement learning lack explicit supervision over the thinking process, causing them to learn suboptimal reasoning strategies that limit generalization.
approach: SophiaVL-R1 trains a thinking reward model to evaluate entire reasoning chains, applies Trust-GRPO to assign trustworthiness weights based on outcome comparisons, and uses an annealing schedule to gradually reduce thinking reward reliance.
contribution: SophiaVL-R1-7B outperforms LLaVA-OneVision-72B on multiple benchmarks despite having 10x fewer parameters.

problem: Diffusion Transformers remain limited by legacy VAE encoders that introduce large convolutional backbones, weak semantic representations, and low-dimensional latent spaces.
approach: Replaces VAE autoencoders with Representation Autoencoders combining pretrained semantic encoders (DINO, SigLIP, MAE) and trained decoders, then proposes theoretically motivated solutions to enable DiTs to operate in high-dimensional spaces.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art image generation with FID 1.18 at 256 resolution and 1.13 at 512 on ImageNet.

problem: Facial expression recognition models struggle with subtle expressions and high inter-subject variability in real-world applications, and source-free domain adaptation is challenged by the scenario of only neutral target expressions.
approach: Personalized Feature Translation operates in latent space, first training on source domain data to transform subject-specific style while preserving expression, then adapting on neutral target data without image synthesis.
contribution: Improves facial expression recognition performance through latent-space feature translation without requiring source data or computationally intensive face image generation.

problem: Long-context LLM inference is computationally expensive due to quadratic attention costs and linear memory overhead, and existing approximate methods rely on coarse token importance predictions.
approach: Uses draft models to precisely predict token and KV pair importance through lookahead, enabling selective KV cache dropping and prompt token compression via attention activations.
contribution: SpecKV and SpecPC methods consistently achieve higher accuracy than baselines while maintaining the same efficiency gains in memory and latency.

problem: Standard reinforcement learning for LLMs relies on average advantage baselines, avoiding expensive value functions that often fail under sparse rewards and long reasoning horizons.
approach: AsyPPO restores the critic role via a set of lightweight mini-critics trained on disjoint prompt shards, uses inter-critic uncertainty to refine policy updates by masking redundant advantages and filtering high-divergence states.
contribution: Achieves >6% performance gains on Qwen3-4B-Base and ~3% on larger models compared to GRPO, improving learning stability.

problem: LLMs are pre-trained on data containing copyrighted and proprietary content, which violates AI legislation requiring compliant, truly open pre-training datasets.
approach: Common Corpus assembles the largest open LLM pre-training dataset by carefully curating uncopyrighted or permissively licensed data spanning diverse languages and domains.
contribution: Contains approximately two trillion tokens with wide language coverage from high-resource European languages to underrepresented low-resource languages, plus significant code data.

problem: Compressed Vision Transformers for edge devices retain substantial class-irrelevant knowledge, resulting in suboptimal performance when only specific classes are needed for deployment.
approach: Vulcan leverages knowledge disentanglement—where FFN modules encode class-specific and MHA captures class-agnostic patterns—by deliberately introducing redundancy through collapsing and low-rank constraints before pruning.
contribution: Derives compact class-specific ViTs that significantly reduce size and computation while even surpassing original ViT performance on target classes.

problem: Diffusion-based language models suffer from high computational overhead by predicting all suffix tokens at each step while retaining only a fraction.
approach: DPad restricts attention to a structured subset of suffix tokens via a sliding window and distance-decay dropout, maintaining fidelity while eliminating redundancy in a training-free manner.
contribution: Delivers up to 61.4x speedup over vanilla diffusion LLMs while maintaining comparable accuracy on long-sequence inference.

problem: Prior system identification methods fail on multi-object scenes with contact-rich interactions because they focus on single objects or discrete material classification.
approach: MOSIV directly optimizes continuous per-object material parameters using a differentiable simulator guided by geometric objectives derived from video observations.
contribution: Substantially improves grounding accuracy and long-horizon simulation fidelity on multi-object contact-rich interactions compared to baselines.

problem: Attention matrix computation in transformers requires Ω(n²) operations to explicitly form the softmax matrix, driving the need for efficient approximations.
approach: Proposes a quantum data structure using quantum Nyström approximation and quantum leverage score sampling to approximate any row of the attention matrix in sublinear time.
contribution: First quantum algorithm approximating attention matrix rows in sublinear time with respect to n.

problem: Quantum data loading remains a bottleneck for quantum computing, as existing approximate quantum loaders are either heuristic or lack general theoretical guarantees.
approach: AQER reformulates AQL methods into a unified framework, establishes information-theoretic bounds on approximation error, and constructs loading circuits by systematically reducing entanglement.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing methods in both accuracy and gate efficiency across synthetic, image, language, and quantum many-body datasets up to 50 qubits.

problem: Current LLM reasoning initiates thinking only after the entire input is available, introducing unnecessary latency and weakening attention to earlier information in dynamic scenarios.
approach: StreamingThinker enables LLMs to think while reading through streaming CoT generation, streaming-constraint training, and parallel KV caches that decouple input encoding from reasoning.
contribution: Achieves 80% reduction in token waiting time and over 60% reduction in latency for final answer while preserving performance comparable to batch thinking.

problem: Sparse autoencoders are computationally expensive and require supervision; extracting interpretable concepts from neural networks in an unsupervised manner remains challenging.
approach: Clusters activation differences justified by discriminant analysis, refines diversity by weighting clusters using activation skewness, aligning with Deleuzian philosophy of concepts as differences.
contribution: Achieves concept quality surpassing prior unsupervised SAE variants while approaching supervised baselines across five models and three modalities.

problem: High Dynamic Range novel view synthesis must handle dynamic scenes with temporal radiance variations, but current methods focus only on static scenes under conventional imaging.
approach: HDR-4DGS uses Gaussian Splatting with an innovative dynamic tone-mapping module that connects HDR and LDR domains while maintaining temporal radiance coherence.
contribution: Achieves both temporal radiance consistency and spatially accurate color translation, enabling photorealistic HDR renderings from arbitrary viewpoints and time instances.

problem: Large language models lack awareness of knowledge boundaries, making it difficult to identify when adaptive inference mechanisms like RAG should be invoked.
approach: Proposes Internal Confidence, a training-free method leveraging self-evaluations across layers and tokens to estimate query-level uncertainty before token generation.
contribution: Outperforms several baselines in detecting knowledge boundaries and enables efficient adaptive inference mechanisms.

problem: Initial noise choice strongly affects video diffusion quality and prompt alignment, but models lack inherent mechanisms to select optimal seeds.
approach: ANSE uses Bayesian Active Noise Selection via Attention (BANSA), measuring entropy disagreement across stochastic attention samples to estimate model confidence.
contribution: Improves video quality and temporal coherence with marginal inference overhead across diverse text-to-video backbones.

problem: Adversarial training is computationally expensive, yet its potential as a foundation for universally robust models remains unexplored theoretically.
approach: Shows that single-layer linear transformers, after adversarial pretraining across diverse tasks, can robustly generalize to unseen tasks through in-context learning.
contribution: Demonstrates that adversarially pretrained transformers can provide free adversarial robustness to downstream tasks despite expensive initial training.

problem: Large language models are vulnerable to hallucinations producing fluent yet unreliable outputs with high variance, requiring reliable uncertainty quantification.
approach: Leverages quantum tensor network-based pipeline for uncertainty quantification accounting for token-sequence probability aleatoric uncertainty in semantic equivalence clustering.
contribution: Detects hallucinations robustly across different generation lengths and quantization levels, showing consistent AUROC and AURAC improvements over baselines.

problem: Diffusion model sampling requires many model evaluations at inference time, and classical ODE multistep methods have inconsistent design choices for prediction types and integration domains.
approach: Dual-Solver generalizes multistep samplers with learnable parameters that interpolate among prediction types, select integration domains, and adjust residuals, trained via frozen classifier feedback.
contribution: Improves FID and CLIP scores in low-NFE regimes across class-conditional and text-to-image generation tasks.

problem: Bridging the sim-to-real gap in robotic grasping remains difficult, especially in learning physics-aware policies from limited human demonstrations.
approach: D-REX uses Gaussian Splat representations to build a differentiable engine for object mass identification from visual observations, enabling force-aware policy learning from human demonstrations.
contribution: Achieves accurate and robust mass identification across object geometries while enabling superior grasping performance with reduced sim-to-real gap.

problem: Existing set representation methods focus on intra-set properties like permutation invariance but poorly model inter-set correlations critical for fine-grained comparisons.
approach: SRAL conceptualizes sets as high-dimensional distributions, uses 2-Sliced-Wasserstein distance for distributional discrepancy encoding, and applies adversarial auxiliary learning with perturbations.
contribution: Achieves consistent effectiveness across retrieval and processing tasks by learning highly discriminative set representations.

problem: Cross-modal biosignal knowledge transfer requires extensive labeled data per modality and task, yet foundation models are computationally expensive to adapt at scale.
approach: BioX-Bridge trains lightweight bridge networks to align intermediate representations between foundation models across modalities, supporting efficient knowledge transfer.
contribution: Enables unsupervised cross-modal knowledge transfer of biosignals with reduced computational overhead compared to knowledge distillation approaches.

problem: Transformers struggle with symbolic planning tasks requiring loops, variable updates, and conditional branching, especially under length extrapolation.
approach: Inserts discrete controller modules with program primitives (ASSIGN, ADD, COMPARE, BRANCH) into Transformer blocks via Gumbel-Softmax selector and compact program state.
contribution: Achieves strong length generalization on algorithmic benchmarks with 20-40 point improvements in longest-length accuracy over baselines.

problem: Adapting LLMs with proxy models typically requires access to output probability distributions, which are often inaccessible or unstable.
approach: KnowProxy trains proxy models with textual knowledge and reasoning elicited from frozen LLMs through prompting rather than probability distributions.
contribution: Achieves competitive or better performance than traditional fine-tuning without requiring direct access to LLM probability distributions.

problem: Mathematical reasoning step quality in training data fundamentally constrains LLM performance, yet existing step expansion methods require powerful external models or high computational costs.
approach: MathFimer decomposes solution chains into prefix-suffix pairs using fill-in-the-middle task, training a specialized model to reconstruct missing intermediate steps.
contribution: Models trained on MathFimer-expanded data consistently outperform those on original data across multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Chart-to-code generation requires complex visual reasoning and structured code output, but supervised fine-tuning plateaus in performance gain despite increasing data.
approach: MSRL employs multi-granularity rewards integrating textual rule-based validation and visual model-based feedback, with two-stage curriculum training progressively incorporating visual signals.
contribution: Breaks the SFT plateau on a 3-million chart-code pair corpus from arXiv, demonstrating substantial improvements from reinforcement learning.

problem: Expressive performance rendering and automatic piano transcription are inverse tasks but have been addressed independently, missing opportunities for joint modeling.
approach: Proposes unified framework jointly modeling both tasks by disentangling note-level score content and global performance style, with diffusion-based style recommendation module.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance on both EPR and APT while enabling effective content-style disentanglement, style transfer, and stylistically appropriate rendering.

problem: Semantic speech tokenizers are fragile to acoustic perturbations, changing output tokens drastically even when speech remains perfectly intelligible.
approach: StableToken uses multi-branch architecture with bit-wise voting consensus mechanism to merge parallel representations into stable token sequences.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art token stability under diverse noise conditions, significantly improving robustness of downstream SpeechLLMs.

problem: Subgroup fairness in presence of multiple sensitive attributes becomes computationally intractable as the number of attributes grows, creating data sparsity.
approach: DRAF reduces surrogate fairness gap for supremum IPM by focusing on subgroups with sufficient sample sizes and marginal fairness via doubly regressing adversarial learning.
contribution: Outperforms baseline methods especially when the number of sensitive attributes is large, with much less computation than directly reducing supIPM.

problem: Distributed clustering must balance communication complexity with approximation quality when data is partitioned across multiple sites.
approach: Designs protocols for constructing (1+ε)-coresets in coordinator and blackboard models using block-diagonal weighted least squares and efficient encoding schemes.
contribution: Achieves communication complexity matching offline coreset constructions and existing lower bounds, improving over prior work by eliminating explicit coordinate communication.

problem: Video generation models struggle to produce temporally coherent and geometrically consistent predictions across multiple camera views.
approach: Enforces multi-view 3D consistency through cross-view pointmap alignment supervision, enabling generation from novel viewpoints without camera pose information.
contribution: Produces visually stable and spatially aligned video predictions that generalize well to novel camera viewpoints for robot manipulation.

problem: Reinforcement learning for diffusion LLMs is challenging because intractable log-likelihood prevents direct application of standard policy gradient methods.
approach: SPG leverages both upper and lower bounds of true log-likelihood for more accurate policy gradient estimation compared to one-sided ELBO approximations.
contribution: Significantly outperforms ELBO-based methods with accuracy improvements of 3.6% on GSM8K, 2.6% on MATH500, 18.4% on Countdown, and 27.0% on Sudoku.

problem: Class incremental learning evaluation using mean and variance from small random sequence samples severely underestimates true performance variance.
approach: EDGE adaptively identifies extreme class sequences using inter-task similarity to characterize the full performance distribution.
contribution: Provides closer approximation of ground-truth performance distribution by capturing performance extremes in class incremental learning.

problem: Arabic remains severely underrepresented in medical NLP, lacking large-scale datasets and benchmarks to evaluate LLM multilingual capabilities.
approach: MedAraBench manually digitizes academic medical materials from Arabic-speaking regions to construct a large-scale QA dataset with expert evaluation and LLM-as-judge assessment.
contribution: Provides large-scale Arabic medical QA benchmark spanning 19 specialties and five difficulty levels to broaden medical AI evaluation diversity.

problem: Large reasoning models trained with reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards excel at objective tasks but degrade diversity, causing failure on subjective reasoning with multiple valid answers.
approach: MultiRole-R1 synthesizes reasoning chains incorporating various role perspectives and uses Group Relative Policy Optimization with diversity-based reward shaping.
contribution: Increases in-domain accuracy by 14.1% and out-of-domain accuracy by 7.64% while also enhancing advanced math reasoning performance.

problem: High-dimensional regression requires effective dimension reduction, but existing approaches may not adaptively select optimal projection directions.
approach: Uses ensemble of random projections with disjoint groups, selects best projection per group by empirical performance, and aggregates via SVD.
contribution: Consistently matches or outperforms state-of-the-art methods across simulated and real datasets through flexible framework.

problem: Dynamic path planning in urban networks requires efficient feature representation balancing completeness with computational cost under rapidly changing traffic.
approach: DFR framework progressively refines global traffic dynamics into compact features using policy attention mechanism to extract top-k paths and intersect with n-hop neighborhoods.
contribution: Guarantees state completeness while significantly improving path planning performance and convergence speed compared to classical baselines.

problem: Exploiting symmetries in tensor-valued functions is essential for efficient learning on scientific data like time series and materials.
approach: Develop universally expressive equivariant architectures on tensors that exploit orthogonal, Lorentz, and symplectic group symmetries; combine with path signatures for time series invariance.
contribution: Equivariant tensor models outperform non-equivariant baselines on materials science, theoretical computer science, and time series problems.

problem: Generating jointly correlated samples from multiple diffusion models while enforcing task-specific constraints without retraining is difficult.
approach: Projected Coupled Diffusion introduces coupled guidance to coordinate diffusion models and adds projection steps to enforce hard constraints at each denoising step.
contribution: PCD enables constrained joint generation for image-pair synthesis, object manipulation, and multi-robot motion planning with guaranteed constraint satisfaction.

problem: ML-based malware detection fails to account for concept drift as Android ecosystems evolve and malware families emerge.
approach: Present LAMDA, a 12-year longitudinal Android malware benchmark with over 1 million samples covering 1,380 malware families to systematically evaluate temporal drift in detection.
contribution: LAMDA quantifies performance degradation of standard ML models over time and enables research into temporal drift, generalization, and evolving detection challenges.

problem: Federated learning is susceptible to source inference attacks where a server identifies which client owns a given data point.
approach: Propose parameter-level shuffling combined with the residue number system in a shuffle model to defend against source inference attacks.
contribution: The method reduces attack accuracy to random guessing levels without affecting model accuracy and integrates seamlessly with other privacy mechanisms.

problem: Single linear dynamical systems fail to capture heterogeneity in neural data where different conditions have variations in dynamics.
approach: Combine tensor-based moment methods for identifiability with EM refinement; construct moment tensors and apply simultaneous matrix diagonalization followed by Kalman filter-smoother EM.
contribution: Hybrid approach provides identifiability guarantees while combining global initialization robustness with flexible latent model fitting for mixtures of LDS.

problem: Understanding logical reasoning failures in LLMs requires grounding error analysis in cognitive theory rather than just reporting error rates.
approach: Use Erotetic Theory of Reasoning and PyETR to generate 383 formally specified reasoning problems and evaluate whether LLM errors match ETR-predicted fallacy patterns.
contribution: Show that higher-capability models exhibit more ETR-predicted fallacies and premise order significantly reduces fallacy production, mirroring human biases.

problem: Red-teaming becomes ineffective once target models exceed attacker capabilities in the weak-to-strong regime.
approach: Frame red-teaming through capability gaps between attacker and target; evaluate over 600 LLM-based jailbreak attacks across diverse model pairs.
contribution: Attack success correlates with capability gap and social science MMLU-Pro performance; derive a jailbreaking scaling curve predicting attack success.

problem: Rotary Position Embedding extension strategies lack unified theory, making it unclear how to generalize RoPE for longer sequences.
approach: Propose MrRoPE, a radix system conversion perspective that unifies RoPE-extension approaches; introduce MrRoPE-Uni and MrRoPE-Pro using uniform and progressive radix strategies.
contribution: MrRoPE-Pro sustains over 85% recall on 128K Needle-in-a-Haystack without fine-tuning and achieves double YaRN accuracy on retrieval tasks.

problem: The internal frequency structure and per-dimension utilization of Rotary Position Embeddings remain poorly understood despite widespread deployment.
approach: Introduce Frequency Entropy metric to quantify effective utilization of each RoPE frequency dimension; analyze Llama-4's RoPE layers systematically.
contribution: Show that high-entropy dimensions are often redundant and can be attenuated at inference with negligible accuracy loss, providing design insights for RoPE.

problem: Current unlearning methods require unlearning targets in the training objective, risking exposure to sensitive data and contradicting privacy minimization.
approach: Propose Partial Model Collapse that leverages distribution collapse from training on model outputs to remove information without explicit unlearning targets.
contribution: PMC removes private information from model outputs while preserving general utility and avoids the privacy risk of explicit unlearning target exposure.

problem: Expensive online RL for theorem proving uses fixed problem sets, causing inefficient training and limiting capability on complex theorems.
approach: GAR jointly trains problem composer and solver in adversarial loop with implicit curriculum learning that aligns task difficulty to prover capability.
contribution: GAR achieves 4.20% relative improvement in pass@32 on MiniF2F-Test and improves DeepSeek-Prover-V2's ProofNet-Test pass@32 from 22.58% to 25.81%.

problem: Learning from irregular, asynchronous temporal data with multiple signal types at different frequencies is challenging.
approach: GMAN is an interpretable framework learning directly from sets of graphs representing sparse heterogeneous signals with node-, graph-, and subset-level importance.
contribution: GMAN achieves state-of-the-art on Crohn's disease onset prediction, hospital length-of-stay, and fake news detection with interpretability.

problem: Existing video reasoning benchmarks lack sufficient depth for extended chain-of-thought reasoning and focus on knowledge rather than visual understanding.
approach: VideoReasonBench depicts sequences of fine-grained operations on latent states visible only partially, evaluating recall, latent state inference, and prediction.
contribution: Comprehensive MLLM evaluation shows most perform poorly on complex reasoning (GPT-4o 6.9% accuracy) while Gemini-2.5-Pro with thinking achieves 56.0%.

problem: For LLM reranking, it is unclear whether contrastive learning or supervised fine-tuning is better and what mechanisms underlie the difference.
approach: Decompose training objectives into weight magnitude and direction components; probe experiments show SFT provides stronger weighting while direction shows no clear winner.
contribution: SFT demonstrates consistent advantage over contrastive learning for LLM reranking through superior weight scheme alignment with generative nature.

problem: Autoregressive LLM inference is fundamentally limited by sequential decoding, requiring efficient alternative approaches.
approach: Fast-dLLM v2 uses block diffusion with complementary attention masking and hierarchical caching (block-level and sub-block) to enable parallel text generation.
contribution: Achieves up to 2.5x speedup over standard autoregressive decoding with only ~1B tokens fine-tuning while matching accuracy.

problem: Formal understanding of why training on chain-of-thought computational traces improves LLM capabilities is limited.
approach: Introduce identification in the limit with trace framework augmenting Gold's paradigm by providing learners with computational traces of accepting machines.
contribution: Perfect traces make computable languages identifiable in the limit, contrasting sharply with Gold's impossibility result for simpler language classes.

problem: Long video understanding with MLLMs requires processing hour-long videos but inflates token budgets beyond practical limits.
approach: FOCUS formulates keyframe selection as combinatorial pure-exploration multi-armed bandit problem, using empirical means and Bernstein confidence bounds.
contribution: Selects less than 2% of video frames while improving accuracy by 11.9% on LongVideoBench for videos longer than 20 minutes.

problem: Self-verification training for LLMs requires sequential generation of solutions and verifications, doubling inference cost.
approach: LaSeR reveals that reasoning reward equals last-token self-rewarding score; augment RLVR loss with MSE loss aligning last-token scores with verifier rewards.
contribution: Joint training of reasoning and self-rewarding provides auxiliary reward signals in both training and testing with reduced inference cost.

problem: Sparse recovery from mixed-quality data sources requires understanding how to trade off high-quality and low-quality measurements.
approach: Establish sample-size conditions for information-theoretic and algorithmic sparse recovery; analyze LASSO in agnostic heterogeneous-noise setting.
contribution: Define Price of Quality trade-off between high and low-quality samples; LASSO threshold matches homogeneous case depending only on average noise.

problem: Efficient tactile data compression for robotic applications under bandwidth constraints is underexplored despite inherent spatiotemporal complexity.
approach: TaCo benchmark evaluates 30 compression methods on tactile datasets; introduce data-driven codecs TaCo-LL (lossless) and TaCo-L (lossy).
contribution: TaCo-LL and TaCo-L codecs outperform existing methods on lossless storage, visualization, material classification, and robotic grasping tasks.

problem: Identifying effective collective variables for accelerated molecular dynamics and rare event sampling remains a major bottleneck.
approach: BioEmu-CV learns CVs from foundation model by training time-lagged generation conditioned on learned CV to capture only slow dynamics.
contribution: Learned CVs enable free energy estimation via enhanced sampling and transition path sampling for fast-folding proteins.

problem: Estimating the optimal (Bayes) classification error is important for understanding how much models can improve.
