approach: Extend soft-label Bayes error estimation to calibrated corrupted soft labels; reveal that calibration alone is insufficient and use isotonic calibration.
contribution: Instance-free method provides statistically consistent Bayes error estimation under weaker assumptions than prior work.

problem: Reasoning video object segmentation with complex text queries fails due to insufficient temporal and spatial integration.
approach: CoT-RVS uses zero-shot chain-of-thought to perform temporal-semantic reasoning: identify matching objects (semantic) and select keyframes (temporal).
contribution: Training-free, MLLM-compatible framework significantly outperforms prior work on both explicit and implicit queries.

problem: Enhancing LLM factuality trades off between flexible non-parametric retrieval (high latency) and parametric fine-tuning (catastrophic forgetting).
approach: MLP Memory pretrain an MLP to imitate k-NN retriever behavior; integrate with Transformer decoders via probability interpolation.
contribution: 12.3% improvement on QA benchmarks, 5.2 points gain on NLP tasks, 10-point hallucination reduction, and 2.5x faster than RAG.

problem: Hard constraints in reinforcement learning degrade policy performance and require intricate reward engineering.
approach: Extend Hamilton-Jacobi RL to dual objectives: Reach-Always-Avoid (RAA) and Reach-Reach (RR); derive explicit Bellman forms via decomposition.
contribution: DO-HJ-PPO outcompetes baselines in success, safety, and speed for safe-arrival and multi-target achievement tasks.

problem: Aligned models gain reasoning but lose creativity and calibration compared to unaligned base models.
approach: Switch Generation trains a switcher LM to guide pretrained and aligned model versions taking turns generating response segments dynamically.
contribution: Model collaboration outperforms individual models on 16/18 tasks with 12.9% average improvement; generalizes to unseen models.

problem: LLMs can detect evaluation settings and adjust behavior, compromising safety evaluation reliability.
approach: Train evaluation-aware LLMs using continued pretraining on type hints and expert iteration; suppress evaluation-awareness via activation steering.
contribution: Steering vectors suppress evaluation awareness and make models act like deployed versions without access to evaluations.

problem: Post-training quantization struggles with outliers in reasoning LLMs where errors accumulate across long chains of thought.
approach: ParoQuant combines Givens rotations with channel-wise scaling to narrow dynamic range; co-design inference kernel for GPU efficiency.
contribution: 2.4% average accuracy improvement over AWQ on reasoning tasks with less than 10% inference overhead.

problem: LLM-based direct move generation for games produces illegal moves and strategically shallow play.
approach: Translate natural language rules into executable Python world models; use code world models with MCTS for high-performance planning.
contribution: Code-generated world models enable verifiable planning, strategic depth via MCTS search, and better generalization to new games.

problem: Cell instance segmentation fails in densely-overlapping regions due to limitations of simple binary graph coloring approaches.
approach: Disco combines data-driven topological labeling with constrained deep learning; use adjacency-aware divide-and-conquer to resolve complex conflicts.
contribution: Framework successfully handles non-bipartite graphs with odd-length cycles and achieves state-of-the-art on GBC-FS 2025 dataset.

problem: LLMs in human-AI collaborative systems struggle to align formal representations with ambiguous natural language, causing hallucinations.
approach: CAPAL learns DFAs with persistent membership noise via class queries; use statistical same-state tests with Hoeffding tolerances.
contribution: Augmented L* loop with class queries enables DFA learning under persistent noise without demonstrations.

problem: Single global linear models fail to capture local relationships that vary across input space regions.
approach: Covariate-guided CLR jointly learns assignment function and K local regressors via alternating minimization with proxy network.
contribution: Method spans spectrum from global to instance-wise fits with convergence guarantees and PAC-style excess-risk bounds.

problem: Geometric generative models on Riemannian manifolds remain computationally expensive at inference despite applications in protein and chemistry.
approach: Generalised Flow Maps extend flow map framework to Riemannian manifolds; instantiate with three self-distillation methods for few-step generation.
contribution: GFMs achieve state-of-the-art sample quality and log-likelihood on geospatial, RNA, and hyperbolic data with single/few-step evaluation.

problem: Attention in diffusion transformers for video generation scales quadratically with sequence length, bottlenecking inference.
approach: DSA integrates sparse attention with distributed inference and carefully-designed parallelism strategies.
contribution: On 8 GPUs, DSA achieves 1.43x speedup over existing distributed methods and 10.79x faster than single-GPU inference.

problem: Reward models lack interpretability and deep reasoning before assigning judgments, limiting alignment quality.
approach: RM-R1 formulates reward modeling as reasoning task with chain-of-rubrics mechanism; train via distillation and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.
contribution: Outperforms larger open-weight (INF-ORM-Llama3.1-70B) and proprietary models (GPT-4o) by up to 4.9% on reward model benchmarks.

problem: Small influential data subsets can overturn model conclusions but lack formal methods to assess if influence is excessive.
approach: Develop framework for most influential sets; derive exact influence formula and identify extreme value distributions (Frechet for constant-size, Gumbel for growing).
contribution: Rigorous hypothesis tests for excessive influence replace ad-hoc heuristics across economics, biology, and ML benchmarks.

problem: Diffusion-based molecular samplers are slower than standard MD and miss thermodynamically relevant modes.
approach: Introduce repulsive potential centered on collective variables from recent samples to encourage exploration of novel CV regions.
contribution: Method recovers diverse conformations, accurate free energy profiles, and demonstrates reactive sampling capturing bond dynamics.

problem: Diffusion-based generative models remain largely opaque despite expanding applications in high-impact domains.
approach: Patronus incorporates prototypical networks to encode visual patch semantics, revealing what patterns are learned and when they emerge.
contribution: Interpretable diffusion models enable shortcut detection and semantic emergence tracing while maintaining strong generative performance.

problem: Limited understanding of why and when test-time training is effective despite growing scale of foundation models.
approach: Under linear representation hypothesis, propose model where foundation models remain underparameterized; TTT enables specialization after generalization.
contribution: Sparse autoencoder experiments confirm key assumptions; scaling studies show TTT specialization most effective in specific parameter regimes.

problem: Knowledge graph foundation models limited by deterministic equivariance, preventing distinction of structurally similar but semantically distinct relations.
approach: Flock leverages probabilistic node-relation equivariance; iteratively sample random walks, encode as sequences, embed with sequence model.
contribution: Universal approximator for isomorphism-invariant link-level functions; achieves state-of-the-art on entity and relation prediction across 54 KGs.

problem: LLMs struggle with long-context question answering when key evidence is dispersed across millions of tokens, especially with methods that process documents in a single forward pass.
approach: ReMemR1 augments memory with callback-enhanced retrieval that allows selective access to the entire history and non-linear reasoning over early evidence, combined with Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Level Rewards (RLMLR) that provides both final-answer and step-level supervision.
contribution: Experiments on long-document QA show significant gains over existing memory-based approaches, validating ReMemR1 as an effective solution for long-context reasoning agents.

problem: Conditioning robot policies on long observation histories is computationally expensive and brittle under covariate shift, while naive subsampling of history leads to irrelevant or redundant information.
approach: MemER employs a hierarchical framework where a high-level policy selects task-relevant keyframes from experience history and uses them with recent frames to generate instructions for a low-level VLA policy, compatible with existing vision-language-action models.
contribution: MemER outperforms prior methods on three real-world long-horizon robotic manipulation tasks requiring minutes of memory.

problem: Existing watermarking methods for detecting and attributing synthetically generated images remain fragile to realistic distortions, susceptible to adaptive removal, and expensive to update when keys change.
approach: Mixture of LoRA Markers (MOLM) formulates watermarking as key-dependent perturbation of generative model parameters using routing-based LoRA adapters, avoiding key-specific retraining while maintaining imperceptibility and robustness.
contribution: MOLM achieves robust key recovery against distortions, compression, regeneration, averaging attacks, and black-box adversarial attacks on Stable Diffusion and FLUX while preserving image quality.

problem: Runtime environments for training cybersecurity LLMs are often unavailable because challenge configurations and execution contexts are ephemeral or restricted, limiting training data generation.
approach: Cyber-Zero leverages publicly available CTF writeups and persona-driven LLM simulation to reverse-engineer runtime behaviors and generate realistic long-horizon interaction sequences without actual environments.
contribution: Cyber-Zero-32B achieves up to 13.1% absolute performance gains over baselines on three prominent CTF benchmarks and matches the capabilities of proprietary systems like DeepSeek-V3-0324 and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.

problem: Guidance signals from annotated data, pseudo-labels, or expert demonstrations can be noisy due to domain shifts or limited availability, causing degraded performance when blindly trusted.
approach: Adaptive Conformal Guidance (AdaConG) dynamically modulates the influence of guidance signals based on their associated uncertainty quantified via split conformal prediction.
contribution: AdaConG improves performance and robustness under imperfect guidance; in gridworld navigation it accelerates convergence and achieves over 6× higher rewards than the best baseline.

problem: EEG foundation models' effectiveness for auditory decoding is constrained by limited integration between neural signals and acoustic stimulus information, hindering generalization across diverse auditory tasks.
approach: MindMix uses two-stage training: pre-training a high-capacity EEG encoder on 3,000+ hours of data, then learning neural-acoustic mapping via a novel Cross-Attention Low-Rank Alignment module for fine-grained cross-modal integration.
contribution: MindMix substantially surpasses existing baselines across auditory attention decoding, auditory emotion recognition, and cross-modal retrieval tasks.

problem: Existing conformal prediction methods for survival time prediction under right-censoring provide only probably approximately correct (PAC) miscoverage guarantees rather than exact ones.
approach: A new calibration procedure under the potential outcome framework uses reweighting to transform the problem into weighted conformal inference, enabling lower prediction bound construction via quantile regression with exact miscoverage guarantees and doubly-robust protection.
contribution: Empirical evaluation on synthetic and real-world clinical data demonstrates the validity and informativeness of the constructed lower prediction bounds.

problem: It remains unclear what properties make tokenizers more effective for generative modeling, and current tokenizers may not align well with downstream denoising objectives used by modern generative models.
approach: Latent Denoising Tokenizer (LDT) aligns tokenizer embeddings directly with the denoising objective by training tokenizers to reconstruct clean images from latent embeddings corrupted via interpolative noise or random masking.
contribution: LDT consistently improves generation quality across six representative generative models on class-conditioned ImageNet and text-conditioned MSCOCO benchmarks compared to prior tokenizers.

problem: Existing change captioning methods operate on static image pairs, ignoring the rich temporal dynamics of the change procedure, which is key to understanding not only what changed but how it occurs.
approach: ProCap reformulates change modeling from static comparison to dynamic procedure modeling using a two-stage design: a procedure encoder learns from automatically-generated keyframes via masked reconstruction, then learnable procedure queries prompt the encoder during captioning.
contribution: Experiments on three datasets demonstrate ProCap's effectiveness in generating descriptions that explicitly describe differences while capturing temporal dynamics.

problem: Scaling RL to real-world applications with multiple, potentially conflicting requirements requires effective constraint satisfaction, but direct policy projection onto feasible regions often lacks stability.
approach: SafeMPO solves a nonparametric surrogate problem guaranteed to contract towards the feasible set, then clones the solution into a neural network policy, improving stability especially during early training when the policy lacks knowledge of constraint boundaries.
contribution: Theoretical results guarantee convergence to the safe set; even the simplest algorithm produces comparable or superior performance compared to highly tuned constrained RL baselines in challenging environments.

problem: Existing OOD generalization methods often underperform on real-world tabular data, while boosting models handle distribution shifts more effectively but the reason is not well understood.
approach: The paper introduces α-predictive sufficiency as an information-theoretic notion and formalizes its link to OOD generalization under hidden confounding, showing that boosting implicitly identifies suitable environments and maximizes predictive performance within them.
contribution: The framework provides theoretical grounding for boosting's success in OOD generalization; validation through synthetic and real-world experiments shows boosting achieves robust performance by identifying environments and maximizing outcome association.

problem: Existing Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) metric solvers for dynamic unbalanced optimal transport are often unstable, computationally expensive, and difficult to scale.
approach: WFR Flow Matching (WFR-FM) is a simulation-free training algorithm that unifies flow matching with dynamic unbalanced OT by simultaneously regressing a displacement vector field and a scalar growth rate function for birth-death dynamics.
contribution: WFR-FM yields more accurate and robust trajectory inference in single-cell biology, reconstructing consistent dynamics with proliferation and apoptosis while outperforming baselines in efficiency and stability.

problem: Machine learning's black-box nature and narrow focus limit adoption by drug discovery experts, while existing LLM methods remain data-intensive and lack transparent reasoning.
approach: DrugTrail integrates structured reasoning trajectories with Druggability-Tailored Preference Optimization (DTPO) to articulate the 'how' and 'why' behind conclusions while balancing binding affinity with other essential druggability factors.
contribution: Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach and its generalizability to a wider range of biomolecular optimization domains.

problem: LLM agents struggle with geometry problem solving due to weak heuristics for auxiliary constructions, and AI methods remain dominated by models relying heavily on large-scale data synthesis.
approach: InternGeometry iteratively proposes and verifies propositions and auxiliary constructions using a symbolic engine and reflects on feedback with a dynamic memory mechanism enabling 200+ interactions per problem, trained with Complexity-Boosting Reinforcement Learning (CBRL).
contribution: InternGeometry solves 44 of 50 IMO geometry problems (2000-2024), exceeding the average gold medalist score (40.9), using only 13K training examples, 0.004% of the data used by AlphaGeometry 2.

problem: Enhancing generative capabilities in multimodal models often comes at the expense of understanding, and vice versa, creating a competitive dynamic within the model.
approach: The Reason-Reflect-Refine (R3) framework reframes single-step generation into a multi-step process of 'generate-understand-regenerate', explicitly leveraging the model's understanding capability during generation.
contribution: R3 successfully mitigates the optimization dilemma, achieving stronger generation results and improved understanding ability related to the generation process.

problem: Handling missing confounders in observational data is challenging, and existing latent variable approaches suffer from consistency issues in causal effect estimation.
approach: CI-StoNet uses a stochastic neural network to jointly model outcome functions and missing confounders with an adaptive stochastic gradient SGHMC algorithm, showing that causal effects remain identifiable even when confounders are non-identifiable.
contribution: CI-StoNet provides state-of-the-art performance on causal effect estimation benchmarks and demonstrates adaptability to proxy variable and multiple-cause scenarios.

problem: Modeling discrete sequences like DNA, proteins, and language requires choosing between three disparate diffusion methods with different algorithms, theoretical structures, and tradeoffs.
approach: A unified theory expresses discrete, Gaussian, and simplicial diffusion as different parameterizations of the Wright-Fisher population genetics model, with simplicial and Gaussian diffusion emerging as large-population limits.
contribution: The theory formally connects likelihoods and hyperparameters; enables training a single model that performs diffusion in any of the three domains at test time while providing stable simplicial diffusion.

problem: Diffusion-based super-resolution is slow at inference and has high memory demands; existing distillation approaches require tile-by-tile processing of high-resolution images due to memory boundaries.
approach: GenDR-Pix eliminates the VAE bottleneck by using pixel-shuffle operations and multi-stage adversarial distillation with generative feature guidance and random padding augmentation.
contribution: GenDR-Pix achieves 2.8× acceleration and 60% memory-saving compared to GenDR with negligible visual degradation and can restore 4K images.

problem: Few-step diffusion distillation typically suffers from format mismatch and quality-diversity tradeoffs due to teachers predicting velocity while students predict shortcuts.
approach: π-Flow modifies the student flow model output layer to predict a network-free policy at one timestep, which then generates dynamic velocities at future substeps via ODE integration, matched to the teacher through imitation distillation.
contribution: On ImageNet 256×256, π-Flow achieves 1-NFE FID of 2.85 outperforming previous 1-NFE models; on FLUX.1-12B and Qwen-Image-20B at 4 NFEs achieves substantially better diversity than state-of-the-art methods.

problem: AI systems frequently exhibit and amplify social biases such as gender, race, and religion bias, requiring methods to identify and correct problematic model weights.
approach: GRADIEND uses an encoder-decoder approach leveraging model gradients to learn feature neurons encoding societal bias information, enabling identification of weights needing change and rewriting to debias models.
contribution: The approach demonstrates effectiveness across various model architectures in identifying bias-related features while maintaining other capabilities.

problem: Designing effective reward functions for complex robotic tasks is challenging, and LLM-generated rewards often produce overly goal-oriented functions that neglect state exploration.
approach: PoRSE (Policy-grounded Synergy of Reward Shaping and Exploration) guides LLMs to generate task-aware rewards while constructing an abstract affordance space for exploration, using in-policy-improvement grounding to dynamically generate and filter reward-bonus pairs.
contribution: PoRSE achieves significant improvement in average returns across robotic tasks compared to previous state-of-the-art methods by fostering mutual reinforcement between reward shaping, exploration, and policy enhancement.

problem: High-quality text is private and cannot be freely used due to privacy concerns, but existing differentially private synthetic text generation imposes uniform guarantees that overprotect non-sensitive content.
approach: Secret-Protected Evolution (SecPE) extends private evolution with secret-aware protection that relaxes Gaussian DP guarantees, enabling tighter utility-privacy tradeoffs while reducing computational complexity.
contribution: Across OpenReview, PubMed, and Yelp benchmarks, SecPE achieves lower Fréchet Inception Distance and higher downstream task accuracy than GDP-based baselines while requiring less noise.

problem: LLMs deployed in applications must reliably refuse malicious prompts and jailbreak attacks, but activation steering methods suffer from a safety-utility tradeoff causing over-refusal on benign prompts.
approach: AlphaSteer learns activation steering with two principled objectives: constructing nearly-zero steering vectors for benign data via null-space constraints for utility preservation, and constructing refusal vectors for malicious data via linear regression for safety enhancement.
contribution: Across multiple jailbreak attacks and utility benchmarks, AlphaSteer significantly improves LLM safety while maintaining performance on benign inputs.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts applied to Diffusion Transformers yields limited gains because visual tokens exhibit spatial redundancy and functional heterogeneity unlike semantic-dense language tokens, hindering expert specialization.
approach: ProMoE features a two-step router with explicit routing guidance: conditional routing partitions tokens into conditional/unconditional sets, and prototypical routing refines assignments via learnable prototypes based on semantic content with a routing contrastive loss.
contribution: ProMoE surpasses state-of-the-art methods on ImageNet benchmark, demonstrating improved expert specialization for vision MoE.

problem: Developing general-purpose 4D world models is constrained by the availability of high-quality data covering dynamic complexity, multi-domain diversity, and spatial-temporal annotations.
approach: OmniWorld combines a newly collected OmniWorld-Game dataset with curated public datasets across diverse domains, providing richer modality coverage and realistic dynamic interactions for training 4D world models.
contribution: Fine-tuning existing methods on OmniWorld leads to significant performance gains on 4D reconstruction and video generation tasks, validating it as a powerful resource.

problem: Existing webpage-to-code benchmarks focus on static screenshot-to-code tasks, overlooking the dynamic interactions fundamental to real-world web applications.
approach: IWR-Bench introduces a benchmark for evaluating LVLMs in interactive webpage reconstruction from video, comprising 113 curated tasks with 1,001 actions from real-world websites and an agent-as-a-judge evaluation framework.
contribution: Experiments reveal that the best LVLM model achieves only 36.35% overall score with functional correctness (24.39%) lagging visual fidelity (64.25%), highlighting critical limitations in reasoning about temporal dynamics.

problem: Encoder-based 3D LMMs face challenges adapting to varying point cloud resolutions and producing point features that don't meet LLMs' semantic needs.
approach: ENEL proposes an encoder-free 3D LMM using LLM-embedded Semantic Encoding with Hybrid Semantic Loss during pre-training and Hierarchical Geometry Aggregation incorporating geometric inductive bias during instruction tuning.
contribution: ENEL's 7B model rivals state-of-the-art 13B models, achieving 57.91%, 61.0%, and 55.20% on classification, captioning, and VQA tasks respectively.

problem: Vision learners with continual learning struggle with catastrophic forgetting due to reliance on class recognition rather than understanding classes as compositions of representative concepts.
approach: CompSLOT guides concept learning across diverse continual learners by extracting semantic slots from vision transformers, using primitive selection and aggregation mechanisms, plus method-agnostic self-supervision to distill concept-based similarity into classifiers.
contribution: CompSLOT significantly enhances various continual learners and provides a universal concept-level module for reducing catastrophic forgetting.

problem: While quantum reservoir computing shows promise for processing temporal data, the approximation capabilities of feedback-based quantum systems remain theoretically unclear.
approach: The paper studies approximation capabilities of recurrent quantum neural networks (quantum analogues of classical RNNs) by projecting regular state-space systems into quantum systems with analysis showing no curse of dimensionality.
contribution: Results show that quantum recurrent neural networks are universal with linear readouts, with qubits growing only logarithmically in the reciprocal of approximation accuracy.

problem: Safe policy improvement offers theoretical control over policy updates in offline tabular RL, but guarantees remain unclear for general online settings combined with world models.
approach: DeepSPI couples local transition and reward losses with regularized policy updates, restricting updates to a neighborhood ensuring monotonic improvement and convergence with analysis linking prediction losses to representation quality.
contribution: On ALE-57 benchmark, DeepSPI matches or exceeds strong baselines including PPO and DeepMDPs while retaining theoretical guarantees.

problem: Ensuring synthesizability in generative small molecule design remains a major challenge, and existing efforts are largely confined to 2D graphs, limiting geometry-based conditional generation.
approach: SynCoGen combines masked graph diffusion and flow matching for synthesizable 3D molecule generation, sampling from the joint distribution of building blocks, chemical reactions, and atomic coordinates using curated SYNSPACE dataset.
contribution: SynCoGen achieves state-of-the-art performance in unconditional molecule generation and competitive performance in zero-shot molecular linker design and pharmacophore conditioning.

problem: Genomics data is often missing in real-world clinical scenarios due to high acquisition cost, and existing reconstruction methods overlook relationships among cases and authentic available data.
approach: MSRL pre-trains a histopathology-genomics multi-modal representation graph using Graph Structure Learning to construct inter-case relevance, then dynamically captures structural relevance during fine-tuning.
contribution: On TCGA datasets with 7,263 cases across survival prediction, cancer grading, and gene mutation tasks, MSRL improves over missing-genomics methods by 1.44% to 3.12% in C-Index.

problem: Existing generative models treat chart editing as pixel manipulation, but charts are structured data representations governed by graphical grammar, not pixel arrangements.
approach: FigEdit introduces a benchmark of 30,000+ samples covering 10 chart types with five progressively challenging tasks (single/multi/conversational/visual-guided edits and style transfer), exposing the limitations of pixel-level approaches.
contribution: Evaluation of state-of-the-art models reveals poor performance on scientific figures and that traditional metrics like SSIM and PSNR have limitations in capturing semantic correctness of edits.

problem: Large language models exhibit high similarity between consecutive layer representations, indicating computational redundancy that can be exploited for layer pruning.
approach: KDP views the LLM forward pass as a discrete-time dynamical system operating on a slow manifold, projects representations into kernel space where transformations become approximately linear, then learns the inverse transformation enabling layer pruning.
contribution: Both theoretical analysis and extensive experiments validate KDP's effectiveness and superiority over existing pruning baselines.

problem: Reasoning under partial observability where key values are missing is challenging, requiring methods beyond traditional latent variable models.
approach: A neuro-symbolic framework treats missing values as latent predicates inferred through logical reasoning, interleaving neural representation learning with symbolic rule induction to discover both conjunctive and disjunctive rules.
contribution: On synthetic and real-world datasets, the framework effectively imputes missing values while uncovering meaningful, human-interpretable rules that govern system dynamics.

problem: Evidential Deep Learning is particularly vulnerable to adversarially perturbed inputs, making overconfident errors despite being designed for uncertainty quantification.
approach: C-EDL (Conflict-aware EDL) generates diverse task-preserving transformations per input and quantifies representational disagreement to calibrate uncertainty estimates without retraining.
contribution: C-EDL significantly outperforms EDL variants and competitive baselines, achieving substantial reductions in coverage for OOD data (up to ~55%) and adversarial data (up to ~90%).

problem: Existing mechanistic interpretability methods rely on flawed activation-magnitude assumptions and are input-centric, failing to capture causal mechanisms driving model outputs.
approach: MICLIP extends CLIP's contrastive learning to align internal mechanisms of vision models with semantic concepts via multimodal alignment between model representations and both input concepts and output semantics.
contribution: MICLIP enables precise causal-aware interpretation of both individual neurons and sparse autoencoder features, revealing semantic properties and enabling targeted manipulation of model behaviors.

problem: Recovering distributions from abundant noisy samples with limited clean samples is challenging when the corruption process introduces per-sample information loss.
approach: SFBD-OMNI formulates distribution restoration as a one-sided entropic optimal transport problem and extends Stochastic Forward-Backward Deconvolution to arbitrary measurement models, providing conditions for recovery.
contribution: SFBD-OMNI substantially improves recovery in the challenging regime of non-identifiable corruption processes, validated through synthetic and real-world experiments.

problem: Traditional cartoon and anime production requires intensive manual effort across keyframing, inbetweening, and colorization stages, with existing methods handling these separately causing error accumulation.
approach: ToonComposer unifies inbetweening and colorization into a single post-keyframing stage using sparse sketch injection and a novel spatial low-rank adapter (SLRA) to adapt a video foundation model to cartoon domain.
contribution: Requiring as few as a single sketch and colored reference, ToonComposer outperforms existing methods in visual quality, motion consistency, and production efficiency.

problem: 3DGS-based avatars struggle with dynamic appearances in loose garments like skirts due to limited Gaussian deformation under template articulation and mismatches with loose apparel geometry.
approach: A motion-aware autoregressive structural deformation framework structures Gaussians into an approximate graph and recursively predicts structure-preserving updates for template-free cloth dynamics.
contribution: The method significantly outperforms existing 3DGS methods in modeling dynamic appearances from single videos, with accurate foreground silhouettes and precise Gaussian alignment.

problem: Flow map models remain unstable and expensive to train, sensitive to hyperparameters even when initialized from pre-trained diffusion models.
approach: Introduces mid-training, a lightweight intermediate stage between diffusion pre-training and flow map post-training that learns trajectory-consistent initialization for vision generation.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art two-step FIDs (1.97 on CIFAR-10, 1.32 on ImageNet 64×64, 1.84 on ImageNet 512×512) using up to 98% less training data and GPU time than prior methods.

problem: Open-ended scientific problem solving is inherently unbounded and domain-specific, requiring exploration across vast solution spaces with limited generalization in existing approaches.
approach: Proposes HELIX, a hierarchical evolutionary reinforcement learning framework combining diverse candidate solutions through in-context learning with iterative RL policy refinement.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on circle packing (sum of radii 2.635983 using 14B model) and surpasses GPT-4o on ML benchmarks with 5.95-point F1 improvement on Adult/Bank Marketing and 40.5% RMSE reduction on Boston Housing.

problem: Federated LLM fine-tuning faces massive memory and communication challenges due to parameter scale, while non-IID data across clients further complicates convergence.
approach: Introduces Meerkat, a sparse zeroth-order optimization method using transferable static parameter subsets with high-frequency communication and virtual path mechanisms to detect extreme Non-IID clients.
contribution: Enables cost-effective federated LLM fine-tuning with superior performance compared to full-parameter zeroth-order baselines and improved handling of data heterogeneity.

problem: Contact forces in robot dynamics introduce discontinuities that severely degrade gradient-based optimization in simulators, creating a trade-off between realism and gradient accuracy.
approach: Proposes DiffMJX coupling adaptive time integration with penalty-based simulation, plus contacts from distance (CFD) using straight-through estimation to preserve pre-contact gradients.
contribution: Substantially improves gradient accuracy under hard contacts and enables informative pre-contact gradients while maintaining physical realism.

problem: PDE surrogate models like FNO and PINN fail to generalize across inputs with diverse physical units and scales, severely limiting out-of-distribution prediction.
approach: Proposes π-invariant test-time projection preserving Buckingham π-invariants via log-space least squares, with clustering to reduce computational complexity from O(MN) to O(KN).
contribution: Achieves average MAE reduction up to 91% across wide input scale ranges on 2D thermal conduction and linear elasticity with minimal overhead.

problem: Small proxy models trained with fixed hyperparameters produce unreliable dataset rankings for pretraining data selection, with conclusions not transferring to large-scale production.
approach: Proposes training proxy models with sufficiently small learning rates to produce dataset rankings that correlate with large-scale optimally-tuned models, with theoretical guarantee via random-feature analysis.
contribution: Demonstrates through 23 data recipes that small-scale ranking reliability can be recovered with proper hyperparameter tuning, preventing costly data selection errors.

problem: Dynamical Similarity Analysis (DSA) ignores how inputs drive dynamics, misclassifying similar systems driven differently—a critical issue for real-world non-autonomous systems.
approach: Introduces InputDSA extending DSA by estimating and comparing both input and intrinsic dynamic operators using Dynamic Mode Decomposition with control (DMDc) based on subspace identification.
contribution: Successfully compares partially observed input-driven systems from noisy data and identifies that high-performing RNNs are dynamically similar while low-performing ones are more diverse.

problem: Large reasoning models produce plausible-sounding but unreliable rationales that fail to reflect their true decision process, undermining trustworthiness and reliability.
approach: Introduces RFEval benchmark with 7,186 instances across seven tasks using controlled output-level counterfactual interventions to probe two testable conditions: stance consistency and causal influence.
contribution: Finds unfaithfulness in 49.7% of outputs from twelve open-source LRMs, reveals that post-training RL can reduce faithfulness despite maintaining accuracy, and proves accuracy is not a reliable proxy for faithfulness.

problem: Existing static agent benchmarks rapidly saturate as agents improve, failing to provide sustained evaluation challenges and limiting ability to assess emerging capabilities.
approach: Proposes TRACE framework where agents freely explore and evolve original benchmark tasks into higher-difficulty variants while recording traceable execution trajectories through evolutionary proposal mining and multi-level validation.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent task complexity enhancement on GAIA benchmark with improved correctness reliability through validatable reproducible trajectories, enabling self-evolving evaluation systems.

problem: Estimating Schrodinger potentials for optimal transport between distributions lacks tight sample complexity guarantees when only observing samples from initial and final densities.
approach: Uses Ornstein-Uhlenbeck reference process with stochastic optimal control to estimate Schrodinger potentials, deriving tight generalization bounds under spectral assumptions via risk minimization.
contribution: Establishes tight bounds on generalization ability achieving fast convergence rates up to logarithmic factors for Schrodinger potential estimation including Gaussian mixtures.

problem: Multi-view 3D generation suffers from poor visual quality while 3D-consistent approaches sacrifice realism, with conventional multi-view paradigm unable to balance these trade-offs efficiently.
approach: Proposes FlashWorld with dual-mode pre-training from video diffusion priors followed by cross-mode post-training distillation that bridges multi-view and 3D-oriented generation while reducing denoising steps.
contribution: Generates high-quality 3D scenes from single image or text in seconds, 10-100x faster than prior works while maintaining superior rendering quality and 3D consistency.

problem: Claims of optimizer speedups are undermined by unequal hyperparameter tuning and limited evaluation, obscuring fair comparisons and hindering practical adoption of alternatives to AdamW.
approach: Conducts systematic study of ten optimizers across four model scales and data-to-model ratios with rigorous hyperparameter tuning and evaluations at training end, revealing matrix-based preconditioners as fastest methods.
contribution: Shows actual speedup of proposed optimizers over well-tuned AdamW decreases with scale to 1.1x for 1.2B models, with matrix-based optimizers (Muon/Soap) being fastest but speedup inversely proportional to scale.

problem: Vision-language models struggle with visual-spatial reasoning because visual tokens are overshadowed by language tokens, preventing consistent recognition of visual cues across frames.
approach: Proposes VideoAnchor, a plug-and-play module leveraging sparse subspace clustering's self-expressiveness property to reinforce visual cues via attention anchoring without retraining.
contribution: Achieves 3.2% and 4.6% improvements on VSI-Bench and Video-MME spatial-related tasks with InternVL2-8B and Qwen2.5VL-72B respectively, demonstrating consistent gains across models.

problem: Understanding how Transformers learn from long, distributional contexts and recall relevant information remains theoretically unclear despite empirical success in content-addressable retrieval.
approach: Recasts Transformer attention as measure-theoretic associative memory where context is a distribution and attention is an integral operator, proving softmax attention trained via empirical risk minimization learns recall-and-predict decomposition.
contribution: Establishes matching minimax lower bounds proving convergence optimality, providing theoretical grounding for Transformer generalization on long distributional contexts.

problem: Existing mechanistic interpretability and circuit discovery rely on manual inspection at toy scale and miss feature interactions through activation-only analysis.
approach: Proposes WeightLens and CircuitLens that analyze features directly from learned weights and capture circuit-level dynamics via transcoders, eliminating need for explainer models or datasets.
contribution: Increases interpretability robustness by going beyond activation analysis to reveal circuit dynamics, enhancing scalable mechanistic analysis while maintaining efficiency.

problem: Visual-prompted object detection lacks research and relies on text-prompted training, leading to suboptimal performance from missing global discriminability in visual prompts despite advantages for rare categories.
approach: Proposes DETR-ViP combining image-text contrastive learning with global prompt integration, visual-textual prompt relation distillation, and selective fusion strategy for robust detection.
contribution: Substantially outperforms state-of-the-art on COCO, LVIS, ODinW, and Roboflow100 benchmarks with enhanced discriminative visual prompt representations.

problem: Multi-agent coordination faces trade-off between capturing diverse behaviors and enabling real-time execution: diffusion methods excel at expressiveness but are computationally slow.
approach: Proposes MAC-Flow learning flow-based representation of joint behaviors then distilling into decentralized one-step policies via flow matching for fast execution.
contribution: Achieves 14.5x faster inference compared to diffusion-based MARL methods while maintaining performance across 12 environments and 34 datasets.

problem: Large-scale TSP remains NP-hard and unsolved efficiently: classical methods don't scale, heuristics need domain tuning, and learning methods generalize poorly with fixed training.
approach: Proposes ViTSP leveraging pre-trained VLMs to visually identify promising small-scale subproblems from TSP visualization, then solving with off-the-shelf optimizer for global improvement.
contribution: Achieves sub-0.2% average optimality gaps on instances up to 88k nodes, surpassing LKH-3 by 12-100% gap reduction especially on very-large-scale instances.

problem: Attribute correlations in training data prevent deep generative models from synthesizing under-represented attribute combinations, limiting diversity in minority samples.
approach: Proposes ProReGen using progressive residual generation inspired by Robinson's transformation to orthogonalize inputs, first learning majority samples then expanding with residual layers for minorities.
contribution: Demonstrates improved synthesis of minority attribute combinations across three benchmark datasets with controlled attribute correlation strengths.

problem: LLMs struggle with safety alignment, facing vulnerability to adversarial attacks and excessive overrefusal on benign sensitive queries, with current safeguards either rejecting outright or providing no guidance.
approach: Proposes WaltzRL, a multi-agent RL framework jointly training conversation and feedback agents as collaborative game where feedback agent provides safety suggestions that improve responses.
contribution: Significantly reduces unsafe responses (from 39.0% to 4.6% on WildJailbreak) and overrefusals (from 45.3% to 9.9% on OR-Bench) compared to various baselines.

problem: Vision-language models face computational overhead from extensive visual tokens, but existing pruning strategies either sacrifice feature diversity or increase hallucination without principled analysis.
approach: Conducts empirical analysis using effective rank for diversity measurement and attention entropy, revealing strengths of attention-based pruning on simple images and diversity methods on complex ones.
contribution: Proposes image-aware hybrid pruning achieving strong performance across benchmarks with reduced hallucination compared to diversity-only approaches.

problem: RL training dynamics in LLMs for reasoning remain unclear, with understanding limited to empirical observation of training trajectory.
approach: Develops theoretical framework via pattern-level and token-level analysis showing RL primarily optimizes sparse critical token subsets, reshaping reasoning pattern distributions under two reward types.
contribution: Explains RL training dynamics showing verifiable rewards enable convergence to optimal strategies when base reasoning is strong, while internal feedback initially improves then potentially degrades performance.

problem: Selective prediction for foundation models faces challenges across open-set taxonomy tasks with unbounded vocabularies: instability in visual-language embeddings and poor similarity calibration.
approach: Proposes memory-augmented PaPSP (MA-PaPSP) augmenting base method with retrieval dataset to reduce embedding variance via averaging nearest-neighbor pairs and using contrastive normalization.
contribution: Outperforms selective prediction baselines across selective captioning, image-text matching, and fine-grained classification tasks.

problem: Reasoning models exhibit overthinking with redundant steps, triggered by internal bias—an implicit preliminary guess about answers formed immediately upon encountering the problem.
approach: Identifies internal bias through empirical observation and counterfactual interventions showing removing input question reduces redundant reasoning and that excessive attention to input drives bias.
contribution: Demonstrates causal relationship between internal bias and overthinking across multiple reasoning models and tasks, though mitigation methods remain ineffective.

problem: Multi-task learning suffers from gradient conflicts causing unfair optimization and degraded performance when tasks have competing gradients.
approach: Proposes SVFair using Shapley value-based framework with geometric conflict metrics (VolDet and VolDetPro) to quantify task deviations and rebalance updates toward fairness.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results across diverse supervised and reinforcement learning benchmarks with controllable complexity.

problem: Understanding how neural networks efficiently learn high-dimensional features in the multi-index model setup remains theoretically open despite empirical success.
approach: Proves that two-layer network trained via layer-wise gradient descent agnostically learns target with o_d(1) test error using O-tilde(d) samples and O-tilde(d^2) time via power-iteration in first layer.
contribution: Demonstrates sample and time complexity align with information-theoretic limits up to leading order, proving optimality and that optimal results require first-layer training beyond O(1) steps.

problem: Fourier Neural Operators (FNO) fail on position-dependent dynamics and have spectral decay assumptions limiting practical applicability to many PDEs.
approach: Introduces KANO using dual-domain parameterization with spectral and spatial bases, including symbolic interpretability that overcomes FNO spectral bottleneck.
contribution: Robustly generalizes on position-dependent operators where FNO fails, reconstructs quantum Hamiltonians in closed-form symbolic representations with ~6e-6 state infidelity, vastly outperforming FNO.

problem: Vision-proprioception policies show inconsistent generalization: during motion-transition phases, the policy suppresses visual learning in favor of faster proprioceptive signals.
approach: Proposes GAP algorithm adaptively modulating proprioceptive gradient magnitude based on phase-guided transition probability estimation, enabling dynamic modality collaboration.
contribution: Demonstrates robust and generalizable vision-proprioception policies in both simulated and real-world robotic manipulation environments.

problem: Data-driven scientific models fail on out-of-distribution data but detecting failures in regression tasks lacks practical solutions, threatening deployment in critical fields.
approach: Proposes OOD detection via score-based diffusion models estimating joint likelihood of inputs and predictions, providing task-aware reliability scores.
contribution: Shows likelihood strongly correlates with prediction error across scientific datasets including PDEs and satellite imagery, providing step toward verifiable certificate of trust.

problem: Value-factorization methods for cooperative MARL lack robustness guarantees under environmental uncertainties from sim-to-real gap and model mismatch.
approach: Introduces DrIGM principle requiring robust greedy actions to align with robust team-optimal actions, deriving robust variants of value-factorization architectures (VDN/QMIX/QTRAN).
contribution: Consistently improves out-of-distribution performance on SustainGym and StarCraft with provable robustness guarantees while preserving scalability.

problem: Training graph neural networks for physical systems via gradient descent is slow, especially for large complex N-body systems, despite needing to respect symmetries.
approach: Replaces iterative gradient-descent optimization with random feature-based parameter construction for Hamiltonian Graph Networks, preserving physical invariances.
contribution: Trains 150-600x faster with comparable accuracy across diverse simulations including systems with up to 10,000 particles, with zero-shot generalization to 4096-node systems.

problem: Optimization on Riemannian manifolds lacks adaptive step-size methods with convergence guarantees without line search, limiting applications like Gaussian variational inference.
approach: Proposes RAdaGD, a family of adaptive gradient descent methods on general Riemannian manifolds achieving non-ergodic convergence guarantee O(1/k) under geodesic smoothness and convexity.
contribution: Provides first convergence guarantee for Gaussian Variational Inference without L-smoothness assumption and demonstrates competitiveness in numerical simulations.

problem: Existing safety benchmarks focus on low-knowledge misuse scenarios or simple classification, failing to assess model safety when handling scientifically sophisticated risks.
approach: Introduces SOSBench benchmark with 3,000 prompts derived from real-world regulations across six high-risk domains (chemistry, biology, medicine, pharmacology, physics, psychology), expanded via LLM-assisted evolution.
contribution: Evaluates frontier models revealing alarmingly high harmful response rates (84.9% for Deepseek-R1, 50.3% for GPT-4.1) demonstrating significant safety alignment deficiencies.

problem: 3D part segmentation only identifies visible surfaces, limiting utility for 3D content creation; extending to complete occluded parts while maintaining global consistency is challenging.
approach: Proposes HoloPart, a diffusion-based model with local attention for fine geometry and global shape context attention, completing incomplete part segments into full 3D parts.
contribution: Significantly outperforms shape completion methods on new ABO and PartObjaverse-Tiny benchmarks, enabling 3D part amodal segmentation for geometry editing and animation.

problem: Existing time series anomaly detection struggles with subtle anomalies like small point anomalies and slowly rising anomalies using reconstruction or prediction methods.
approach: Proposes CS-LSTMs combining noise decomposition strategy with contextual dependencies and seasonal patterns, integrating time and frequency domain representations.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets, demonstrating effectiveness for robust time series anomaly detection.

problem: Most RL methods flatten return distributions to scalars, missing fine-grained structure of future returns and limiting applications in exploration and safe RL.
approach: Uses flow-based models to estimate full return distributions via flow-matching objective satisfying distributional Bellman equation, identifying high-uncertainty states via flow derivatives.
contribution: Achieves 1.3x improvement on average success rates across 37 state-based and 25 image-based benchmarks compared to prior distributional RL methods.

problem: Pedestrian trajectory modeling emphasizes social dynamics while neglecting environmental context, limiting realism in crowd simulation.
approach: Proposes EnvSocial-Diff, a diffusion-based model with structured environmental conditioning (obstacles, objects, lighting) and graph-based individual-group interaction module.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art on multiple benchmarks, demonstrating importance of explicit environmental conditioning and multi-level social interaction.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts models vary in local routing consistency—how well consecutive tokens activate similar experts—limiting understanding of which models suit expert offloading.
approach: Proposes two metrics: Segment Routing best Performance (SRP) and Segment Cache best Hit rate (SCH) to measure local routing consistency across 20 MoE LLMs.
contribution: Reveals trade-off between local routing consistency and local load balance, identifies domain-specialized experts contribute more than vocabulary-specialized ones.

problem: Current safety alignment methods rely on superficial refusal shortcuts or intensive supervision, failing to leverage LLMs' latent safety understanding developed during pretraining.
approach: Proposes AlphaAlign, a pure RL framework with dual-reward system: verifiable safety reward for justified refusals and normalized helpfulness reward, incentivizing proactive safety reasoning.
contribution: Enhances harmful content refusal while reducing overrefusal and maintaining task performance through explicit safety rationales, demonstrating simple pure-RL effectiveness.

problem: Solving infinite-horizon general-utility MDPs in single-trial regime—where performance evaluated on single trajectory—lacks practical solutions despite theoretical importance.
approach: Provides fundamental results on single-trial policy optimization including optimal policy class, casts as equivalent MDP, and leverages Monte-Carlo tree search for planning.
contribution: First approach solving GUMDPs in single-trial regime with superior performance to relevant baselines in experimental settings.

problem: Current language model decoding methods produce repetitive outputs when combined with sampling techniques, limiting the diversity of generated text.
approach: OverRIDE dynamically adjusts decoding by fine-tuning auxiliary output heads on previously generated sequences to suppress semantic patterns that have already appeared, allowing the model to explore new directions while maintaining quality.
contribution: Increases output diversity while maintaining quality across code, math, and story generation with only 6.4% throughput loss on 72B models.

problem: Existing AI security benchmarks are small-scale and measure only static outcomes, failing to capture the dynamic complexity of real-world cybersecurity challenges that require agents to reason about vulnerability chains.
approach: CyberGym presents a large-scale benchmark with 1,507 real vulnerabilities across 188 projects, tasking agents to generate proof-of-concept exploits from vulnerability descriptions and code, with adjustable settings for different analysis scenarios.
contribution: Top-performing agents achieve ~20% success rate, discovered 35 zero-day vulnerabilities and identified 17 historically incomplete patches, demonstrating both benchmark rigor and real-world security impact.

problem: Modern LLMs produce highly human-like text, raising urgent concerns about misinformation and academic integrity without reliable detection methods.
approach: Presents a geometric framework for rewrite-based detection, then introduces a novel algorithm that adaptively learns distance functions between original and rewritten text, theoretically shown to outperform fixed-distance approaches.
contribution: Achieves 57.8–80.6% relative improvements over strongest baselines across different target LLMs (GPT, Claude, Gemini).

problem: Existing 3D colorization methods enforce multi-view consistency by averaging colors, sacrificing both chromatic richness and user control while remaining limited to static scenes.
approach: Color3D colorizes a single key view, then trains a personalized colorizer that propagates its learned scene-specific color mapping to novel views and video frames via Gaussian splatting, enabling diverse yet consistent results.
contribution: Delivers visually diverse, user-controllable colorization with cross-view and cross-time consistency for both static and dynamic 3D scenes.

problem: Single-agent Medical LVLMs struggle to generalize across diverse medical specialties, and existing multi-agent frameworks use fixed static pipelines that lack flexibility and adaptability.
approach: MMedAgent-RL uses reinforcement learning to enable dynamic, optimized collaboration between a triage doctor and specialist agents, with curriculum learning to progressively teach the attending physician to balance specialist input with its own judgment.
contribution: Achieves 23.6% average performance gain over strong baselines on five medical VQA benchmarks, with Qwen2.5-VL agents outperforming proprietary Med-LVLMs.

problem: Multimodal LLMs remain computationally expensive due to quadratic complexity of processing vision tokens, and existing progressive pruning methods misunderstand layer roles and use rigid pruning schedules.
approach: HiDivDrop introduces Late Injection to bypass shallow layers and feed tokens directly to fusion layers, plus a Concave Pyramid Pruning scheme with Early Exit that dynamically adjusts rates via inter-layer similarity and differentiable top-k operations.
contribution: Compresses ~90% of vision tokens while matching original performance and accelerating training by 1.72x.

problem: Safety-critical deep RL requires policies that are both high-performing and safe throughout training, but existing model-predictive shielding is computationally intractable for high-dimensional nonlinear systems.
approach: RAMPS leverages a learned linear representation of environment dynamics to enable robust multi-step Control Barrier Functions that account for model error and delays, providing efficient real-time safety interventions.
contribution: Significantly reduces safety violations compared to existing safe RL methods while maintaining high task performance in complex control environments.

problem: Multi-turn medical dialogues require effective information seeking under uncertainty, but conventional RL methods struggle with long-horizon credit assignment in interactive scenarios.
approach: ATPO adaptively allocates rollout budget to uncertain states via Bellman error and action-value variance, with uncertainty-guided pruning and asynchronous KV-cache-reusing search to mitigate computational cost.
contribution: Qwen3-8B surpasses GPT-4o on medical dialogue benchmarks with +0.92% accuracy improvement and more efficient reasoning.

problem: Developing effective agentic search systems is challenging due to lack of high-quality training data reflecting the complexity of real-world multi-source research tasks.
approach: InfoSeek conceptualizes agentic search as Hierarchical Constraint Satisfaction, using a Diffusion–Retrospection process to generate constraint trees from seed webpages, then sample and blur them to create training instances.
contribution: First publicly released framework for agentic search data synthesis with open-source code and curated datasets, substantially improving performance on diverse information-seeking benchmarks.

problem: Cross-view localization methods rely on global descriptors or BEV transformations, lacking interpretability and fine-grained correspondence understanding for accurate 3DoF pose estimation.
approach: Loc² learns ground–aerial image-plane correspondences from weak pose supervision, lifts matched points into BEV with monocular depth, and applies scale-aware Procrustes alignment for rotation, translation, and scale estimation.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in cross-area testing and unknown orientation scenarios with strong interpretability and outlier rejection via RANSAC.

problem: Graph Transformers struggle to apply to relational entity graphs due to poor generalization of positional encodings to massive heterogeneous graphs and inability to model temporal dynamics and schema constraints.
approach: RelGT employs multi-element tokenization decomposing each node into features, type, hop distance, time, and local structure, combining local attention over subgraphs with global attention to learnable centroids.
contribution: Matches or outperforms GNN baselines by up to 18% across 21 RelBench tasks, establishing Graph Transformers for Relational Deep Learning.

problem: Optimization under heavy-tailed noise (bounded p-th moment, p∈(1,2]) requires better convergence rates than existing Clipped SGD analyses provide.
approach: Provides refined analysis of Clipped SGD with improved rates utilizing Freedman's inequality and introducing generalized effective dimension concept.
contribution: Offers faster convergence rates: O(σₗdₑff^(-1/2p)ln^(1-1/p)(1/δ)T^(1/p-1)) for nonsmooth convex and O(σₗ²dₑff^(-1/p)ln^(2-2/p)(1/δ)T^(2/p-2)) for strongly convex problems.

problem: Digital watermarking for diffusion models introduces distributional shifts and quality degradation, and existing lossless methods require per-image cryptographic overhead.
approach: Spherical Watermark mixes watermark bits with random padding into high-entropy codes, projects them onto the unit sphere via orthogonal rotation, and scales by chi-square-distributed radii to recover exact Gaussian noise.
contribution: Preserves Gaussian priors up to third-order moments, maintains high visual fidelity while improving traceability, computational efficiency, and robustness against attacks.

problem: High-resolution monocular geometry estimation requires balancing global context and fine detail with manageable computational cost, and high-quality supervision is scarce.
approach: Hyden pairs a low-resolution Vision Transformer for global context with a full-resolution CNN for fine details, fusing via lightweight MLP, and uses self-distillation with pseudo-labels from both full-image and high-resolution crops.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on high-resolution benchmarks with lowest inference latency among competitors.

problem: Lipschitz-based certification for robustness has struggled to scale to billion-parameter models and maintain strong ImageNet performance.
approach: LipNeXt introduces constraint-free, convolution-free 1-Lipschitz architecture using manifold optimization on orthogonal manifolds and Spatial Shift Modules for pattern modeling without convolutions.
contribution: Scales to 1–2B models on ImageNet, improving certified robust accuracy by up to 8% at ε=1 over prior Lipschitz methods while enabling efficient low-precision training.

problem: Inductive Knowledge Graph Reasoning with unknown entities and relations struggles to balance LLM knowledge with sparse KG context, and LLM hallucinations undermine reasoning credibility.
approach: KRLM introduces a Knowledge Reasoning Language instruction format and custom tokenizer to align LLM knowledge with KG representations, uses KRL attention layers for dynamic coordination, and applies structure-aware entity prediction to constrain hallucinations.
contribution: Achieves unified coordination between LLM knowledge and KG context, strictly constraining reasoning results within trustworthy domains.

problem: Multimodal reasoning models tend to overthink simple problems with unnecessarily long traces while under-exploring difficult ones.
approach: ARES uses high-window-entropy tokens to identify reasoning-critical moments, then trains with adaptive cold-start on difficulty-proportional traces and Adaptive Entropy Policy Optimization using hierarchical rewards with dynamic KL control.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance and reasoning efficiency across mathematical, logical, and multimodal benchmarks while closing the gap to commercial systems.

problem: Personalizing text-to-image diffusion models leads to overfitting and distributional drift, where models ignore prompts and replicate reference images rather than balancing subject fidelity with text alignment.
approach: Introduces Lipschitz-based regularization during personalization to constrain parameter updates and preserve the pretrained distribution, promoting consistency while enabling accurate concept adaptation.
contribution: Achieves superior performance in visual fidelity and prompt adherence through bounded deviation from original distribution, with computational efficiency over resource-intensive sampling.

problem: Time series forecasting methods rely on complex model structures and strong assumptions about decomposition, limiting robustness and scalability.
approach: Numerion leverages the insight that characteristic frequencies naturally decrease in complex and hypercomplex domains, creating multiple Real-Hypercomplex-Real MLPs to independently model series in different hypercomplex spaces, then adaptively fuses patterns.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art forecasting results on multiple public datasets through natural series decomposition and adaptive fusion of multi-dimensional representations.

problem: Test-time computing in LLMs increases performance but the relationship between model capability, query complexity, and optimal budget allocation remains poorly understood for compute-efficient inference.
approach: Sonata uses self-consistency (agreement among multiple reasoning paths) as a proxy for thinking necessity, training a lightweight adapter offline to predict self-consistency from hidden representations during prefilling, then dynamically allocating thinking budgets.
contribution: Optimizes performance-efficiency tradeoff with <1‰ computational overhead, generalizes across diverse tasks, and enables further gains when combined with CoT compression methods.

problem: Existing multimodal embeddings remain inherently discriminative, limiting their ability to benefit from reasoning-driven generation paradigms and leverage generative reasoning capabilities.
approach: UME-R1 unifies embedding tasks within a generative paradigm via two-stage training: supervised fine-tuning for reasoning capabilities, then RL to enhance quality; discriminative and generative embeddings are complementary.
contribution: Significantly outperforms conventional discriminative embeddings on MMEB-V2 benchmark across 78 video, image, and visual document tasks, with oracle performance far exceeding either embedding type alone.

problem: Few-shot learning methods overlook progressive alignment between vision and language across different semantic levels, limiting semantic gains from LLM integration.
approach: DVLA-RL introduces Dual-level Semantic Construction that generates both fine-grained attributes and high-level descriptions from class names and samples, then uses RL-gated attention to dynamically integrate dual semantics across layers.
contribution: Achieves new state-of-the-art performance with class-specific discrimination and generalized representations from few support samples through precise cross-modal alignment.

problem: Latent thinking in LLMs lacks interpretability and supervision, raising concerns about correctness and reliability of latent reasoning processes.
approach: Reveals that latent thoughts for correct versus incorrect answers exhibit distinguishable patterns, then proposes Latent Thinking Optimization using a latent classifier as a Latent Reward Model to optimize reasoning processes.
contribution: LRM reliably detects incorrect latent thinking and LTO significantly improves reasoning processes, with generalization across domains and seamless application to general LLMs.

problem: Long-form chain-of-thought reasoning in LLMs remains largely an English-centric capability, with unclear transfer to non-English languages.
approach: Systematically investigates four development stages across nine target languages: scaling, pretraining, post-training, and inference, comparing En-CoT and Target-CoT reasoning modes.
contribution: Reveals that broad multilingual pretraining improves both reasoning modes, translated training data outperforms target-language distillation, and identifies language-specific CoT failure modes.

problem: Deep neural RL policies are unstable to minor state variations, and recent ε-local invariance training techniques break counterfactual value learning.
approach: Provides theoretical analysis revealing that ε-local invariance enforcement causes policies to lose counterfactuality and learn misaligned, inconsistent values.
contribution: Demonstrates that standard RL inherently learns counterfactual values and highlights a fundamental gap between biological inspiration and artificial agents trained via ε-local invariance methods.

problem: Chess transformers employ varying architectural designs and unintuitive tokenization schemes that hinder interpretability and human-AI interaction.
approach: Chessformer uses chessboard squares as input tokens, dynamic positional encodings adapted to chess geometry, and attention-based policy output design.
contribution: Advances state-of-the-art in chess playing, human move-matching prediction with smaller models, and enables substantial interpretability benefits through domain-adapted architecture.

problem: Autoregressive image generation predicts tokens in fixed raster-scan order, relying on human-designed prediction units and orders that limit performance.
approach: BAR conceptualizes tokens as basis vectors and employs end-to-end learnable transformation matrix to refactor token sequences, discovering effective generation strategies beyond hand-crafted assumptions.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art FID of 1.15 on ImageNet-256, overcoming human biases and advancing image generation including text-to-image synthesis.

problem: Different transformer attention architectures yield apparently distinct modular addition circuits, but their relationship remains unclear.
approach: Identifies all neurons per learned representation and studies them collectively as manifolds using topological tools, revealing geometric and topological equivalence between circuits.
contribution: Demonstrates that uniform and trainable attention architectures implement the same algorithm via topologically equivalent representations across hundreds of circuits.

problem: Traditional RAG approaches struggle to capture intricate associative patterns and relationships embedded within large document collections.
approach: BrowseNet transforms unstructured text into graph-of-chunks with semantic embeddings and lexical relationships, dynamically traversing query-specific subgraphs to emulate content-addressable memory.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art exact match performance over graph-based RAG approaches and dense retrieval methods.

problem: Existing LLM deception evaluations remain limited to single-turn prompts, failing to capture long-horizon deceptive strategies in extended interactions.
approach: LH-Deception simulates multi-agent systems with performer and supervisor agents across interdependent tasks with dynamic pressures, plus an auditor analyzing full trajectories.
contribution: Finds deception is model-dependent, increases with event pressure, erodes supervisor trust, and reveals emergent long-horizon phenomena like chains of deception invisible to static evaluations.

problem: Generative image models frequently fail to produce seemingly simple concepts (hands, objects in groups of four) present in training data, but these failures are largely documented anecdotally.
approach: Uses sparse autoencoders to extract interpretable concept embeddings from DINOv2 features, enabling quantitative comparison of concept prevalence between real and generated images.
contribution: Identifies specific suppressed blindspots (bird feeders, DVD discs, whitespaces) and exaggerated blindspots (wood texture, palm trees) across four popular models, plus memorization artifacts.

problem: EEG tokenization for foundation models remains challenging, as existing methods operate on strict multi-channel configurations lacking generalization.
approach: TFM-Tokenizer learns time-frequency motif vocabularies from single-channel EEG via dual-path architecture with time–frequency masking, supporting both lightweight transformers and existing foundation models.
contribution: Achieves up to 11% improvement in Cohen's Kappa on diverse benchmarks, consistently boosts diverse foundation models, and generalizes across device types and signal formats.

problem: Large reasoning models incur substantial computational costs for deep reasoning, and existing RL methods struggle to construct short reasoning paths.
approach: Just-Enough Thinking performs trajectory truncation during rollout to expose models to short reasoning paths, using quality-controlled length rewards to encourage conciseness.
contribution: Delivers 4.6% accuracy improvement while reducing output length by 46.3% on Olympiad benchmark using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B.

problem: Scaling continuous-time consistency models to large-scale text-to-image and video diffusion faces infrastructure challenges in Jacobian computation and quality limitations in fine-detail generation.
approach: Develops FlashAttention-2 JVP kernel for parallel training, proposes score-regularized consistency model incorporating score distillation as regularizer to complement forward-divergence objective.
contribution: Scales to 14B models and 5-second videos, matches state-of-the-art DMD2 on quality while mitigating mode collapse and improving diversity without GAN tuning.

problem: Large reasoning models' chain-of-thought reasoning often contains harmful content that persists even when final responses appear safe, undermining trustworthiness.
approach: Proposes Intervened Preference Optimization using process supervision, substituting compliance steps with safety triggers and constructing preference pairs with strong signals for safe reasoning.
contribution: Remarkably improves overall safety regarding both reasoning and responses, with >30% relative reduction in harmful content over SFT and RL baselines.

problem: Graph domain adaptation using discrete strategies fails in real-world scenarios where graph structures evolve continuously and nonlinearly.
approach: DiffGDA models domain adaptation as continuous-time generative process via SDEs, jointly modeling structural and semantic transitions while a domain-aware network steers evolution toward target domain.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines on 14 graph transfer tasks across 8 datasets, theoretically showing diffusion process converges to optimal solution.

problem: EEG spatial super-resolution is hindered by distribution shift and signal distortion when recovering high-density signals from sparse measurements.
approach: SRGDiff uses step-aware residual-guided diffusion where dynamic residual conditions predict step-wise temporal and spatial details, with step-dependent affine modulation steering high-density recovery.
contribution: Achieves consistent gains up to 40% over baselines across signal, feature, and downstream metrics on multiple upsampling scales.

problem: Spatio-temporal reasoning in VLMs remains opaque, with unclear understanding of how visual and textual representations combine for spatial reasoning.
approach: Identifies linear binding of spatial IDs to textual activations and shows reasoning occurs via language tokens, demonstrating through causal interventions that spatial IDs mediate intermediate beliefs.
contribution: Reveals linear spatiotemporal ID mechanism in VLMs, extends analysis to video VLMs identifying temporal IDs, providing diagnostic tool for model limitations.

problem: Effects of compression (quantization, distillation, pruning) on large reasoning models' capabilities remain poorly understood.
approach: Benchmarks quantized, distilled, and pruned DeepSeek-R1 on four reasoning datasets, adapts difference of means and attribution patching to interpret fine-grained causal relationships between weights and reasoning.
contribution: Dynamically quantized 2.51-bit R1 reaches near-R1 performance; reveals weight count impacts memorization more than reasoning, and final-layer MLPs are critical for distilled LRMs.

problem: Mobile GUI agents face environmental injection threats from adversarial UI elements inserted into dynamic on-device ecosystems, bypassing textual safeguards.
approach: GhostEI-Bench assesses mobile agents under environmental injection attacks within dynamic, executable Android environments with fine-grained failure analysis via judge LLM reviewing trajectories.
contribution: Comprehensive evaluation reveals state-of-the-art agents' profound vulnerability to environmental injection, identifies precise failure points in perception, recognition, or reasoning.

problem: Video generation models lack awareness of which objects actors should interact with, limiting their ability to perform directed human-object interactions.
approach: Introduce target awareness by encoding target mask spatial information via a special token in text prompts, then fine-tune with cross-attention loss aligning attention maps to the target mask.
contribution: A target-aware video diffusion model that accurately generates videos of actors performing directed actions on specified objects and enables zero-shot 3D HOI motion synthesis.

problem: Multiple small language models exist but lack orchestration, with each excelling at specific tasks yet individual models underperforming on complex reasoning.
approach: Propose a three-stage orchestration: multi-model architecture coordinating SLMs, model selection search identifying complementary models, and test-time scaling tailored to SLM-MUX.
contribution: SLM-MUX achieves up to 13.4% improvement on MATH, 8.8% on GPQA, and 7.0% on GSM8K, with two SLMs outperforming Qwen 2.5 72B on some benchmarks.

problem: Evaluating video understanding models is challenging since BLEU, ROUGE, and BERTScore fail to capture human judgment nuance, yet obtaining manual evaluations is costly.
